key_finding: This is a pre-study to develop a German preference-based value set for the EQ-5D-5L.
The Personal Utility Functions approach is feasible for directly eliciting individual preferences about EQ-5D dimensions and can be aggregated to generate a social value set.

EQ-5D-5L demonstrates promising psychometric properties in post COVID patients with sensitivity to distinguish health state variations, though mobility and usual activities dominate in explaining general health, suggesting potential value of bolt-on dimensions.

No existing generic preference-based health-related quality of life measure satisfies all criteria for children under seven years, indicating a need to develop a comprehensive proxy instrument with observable behavioral domains and psychometrically sound scoring systems.

Long COVID results in significant HRQoL impairment (EQ-5D-5L index 0.856 pre-COVID to 0.488 at enrolment), with poorer symptoms in more deprived areas, but little difference in HRQoL across deprivation quintiles, with variable patterns between Māori and non-Māori populations.

Routine collection of EQ-5D PROMs can inform patients about expected outcomes from total knee arthroplasty to improve shared decision-making and reduce unnecessary surgery in patients with moderate pain.
An EQ-5D-3L value set and crosswalk EQ-5D-5L value set were successfully created for Bermuda using a DCE-cTTO hybrid valuation protocol to support health policy and clinical decision-making.

Approximately 30% of respondents distinguished between full health and 11111, with sensory deprivation (vision and hearing) and mental health identified as important health aspects not captured by the five EQ-5D dimensions.

Design principles for clinical dashboards incorporating generic (EQ-5D) and disease-specific PROMs should include patient data, clinical metrics, past PROM scores, and peer-group comparisons to support clinician decision-making and early identification of health-related quality of life changes.

conditions: functional abdominal pain not otherwise specified
key_finding: Both EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrated feasibility as outcome measures in pediatric gastroenterology, with the 5L version showing superior discriminatory power compared to the 3L version.
Examination of variability and reliability of EQ-HWB-S and EQ-5D-5L in dementia patients experiencing health fluctuations.

EQ-5D was used in 13.1% of African HRQoL studies, but only 20.3% of EQ-5D studies reported all three components (descriptive profile, index scores, and EQ-VAS), revealing significant inconsistencies in reporting practices.

EQ-5D-5L bolt-ons demonstrate superior psychometric performance compared to 3L versions in both general population and myasthenia gravis patients, with vision and breathing bolt-ons particularly improving sensitivity to MG-related health issues.
Interactions between EQ-5D health domains are important in valuation studies and not accounting for them results in biased QALY tariffs, particularly in stand-alone DCE with duration studies.
Simplified non-linear multiplicative regression models with 8, 9, and 11 parameters outperformed the conventional 20-parameter additive model in predicting out-of-sample EQ-5D-5L health state values.

TTO and DCE preferences show reasonably strong association across EQ-5D-5L dimensions but poor agreement at the individual health state level, suggesting joint modeling approaches should assume association rather than agreement.
A Portuguese EQ-5D-5L value set was successfully estimated using composite time trade-off and discrete choice experiment methods, with interval GLS censored at 1 showing the best model performance.
A workshop was developed to improve routine PROM data collection by engaging patients in shared decision-making using the EQ-5D within clinical contexts.

Shrinkage estimators reduce mean square error and mean absolute error in EQ-5D health utility estimation, particularly benefiting resource-constrained countries with small valuation study sample sizes.

Dimensionality analysis identified seven factors (physical functioning, psychological symptoms, energy/sleep, physical pain, social functioning, needs, and satisfaction) to inform candidate bolt-on dimensions for the EQ-5D-5L.

Physical inactivity and obesity in combination are associated with higher probability of problems across most EQ-5D dimensions, while individual behavioural risk factors show varying associations with specific dimensions.
Discrete choice experiments are feasible in children but children show significantly higher choice blindness rates (35%) compared to adults (9%), though illogical preference rates are similar.
EQ-5D-3L, PASI, and DLQI measure different constructs in psoriasis patients and should be used as complementary measures to comprehensively assess disease impact and health-related quality of life.

First logically consistent TTO-based EQ-5D-3L value set for Slovenia and first monotonic VAS value set in Central and Eastern Europe, with substantial differences from Polish and UK value sets particularly for mobility dimension.

A systematic qualitative review mapping the concepts of health-related quality of life, quality of life, and wellbeing to understand commonalities, differences, and coverage by the EuroQol family of instruments and other generic measures.

The EQ-5D-5L demonstrates feasibility, reliability and validity in Ethiopian stroke patients with strong patient-proxy agreement on utility scores at baseline and follow-up visits, though lower agreement was observed for pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression dimensions.
To develop a value set for the EQ-5D-5L based on societal preferences in Egypt for use in economic evaluation and resource allocation decisions.
The Bangla version of EQ-5D-Y-3L demonstrated strong feasibility and reliability in both self-complete and parent-proxy formats for measuring health-related quality of life in Bangladeshi children.
A research exchange program enhanced expertise in EQ-5D and PROMs applications in clinical practice and health systems, with focus on promoting routine PROMs data collection in healthcare systems.

A Dutch value set for EQ-5D-Y-3L was derived, revealing systematic differences between proxy-proxy and proxy-substitute preference perspectives, with lower valuations for states involving pain and emotional distress in proxy-proxy preferences.

People with self-reported health impairments do not have significantly different EQ-5D-5L health state preferences than the German general population, with only marginal deviations in value sets across subgroups.
Garbage class mixed logit models provide an automated and reliable alternative to manual screening for low-quality DCE respondents with performance comparable to root likelihood tests.

age_group: 0-15 years (infants, toddlers, young children aged 2-4 years, and adolescents aged 13-15 years)
key_finding: This study aims to understand how EuroQol instruments transition across different age groups (EQ-TIPS to EQ-5D-Y Adapted to EQ-5D-Y to adult EQ-5D) and compare their psychometric performance to enable coherent measurement of health-related quality of life across the lifespan.

Level overlap combined with color coding significantly improves attribute attendance and choice consistency in complex discrete choice experiments, with the combination resulting in nearly full attribute attendance and 30% increase in choice consistency.
statistical_methods: heteroskedastic attribute non-attendance mixed logit models

key_finding: A parsimonious optimal scaling approach enables estimation of interaction effects in EQ-5D health state valuation, revealing strong interactions between domains with decreasing marginal effects.

Routine use of PROMs including EQ-5D-5L did not substantively improve patient-clinician communication in hemodialysis units, but had potential to identify and prompt management of mental health concerns.
Investigation of whether an extensive pilot phase in EQ-5D-5L valuation studies improves interviewer protocol compliance, data quality, and reduces interviewer effects and response clustering.
This PhD project aims to compare statistical models for analyzing EQ-5D-5L data in randomized clinical trials to estimate treatment effects and derive health utilities for economic modeling.

This simulation study evaluates design efficiency improvements from seven different DCE design update strategies to determine whether the EuroQol Group should move from a one-design-fits-all approach to sample-specific or automated design updates for EQ-VT valuation studies.
Choice task randomization in split-triplet DCE increases complexity and diverges from cTTO benchmarks, while supplemental pairwise tasks improve anchoring and reliability of value sets.

age_group: children and adults across different age groups
key_finding: This PhD explores how public preferences for health gains differ by age group and whether child QALYs derived from EQ-5D-Y valuation can be compared to adult QALYs, with implications for age-weighted QALY applications in cost-effectiveness analysis.
The difference between children's and adults' cTTO valuations is explained by differences in time preferences rather than true differences in health state utilities.
Cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of EQ-TIPS-3L and EQ-TIPS-5L in Brazilian toddlers and infants to support health-related quality of life assessment in economic evaluations.

Latent class analysis of health valuation preferences identified three distinct taste classes with different priorities regarding quality of life versus life span, with education level associated with class membership.
Systematic review to synthesize evidence on the psychometric properties of the EQ-5D-Y across different clinical areas and identify gaps for future research.
The EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S demonstrate strong psychometric properties including convergent validity, known-group validity, test-retest reliability, and responsiveness in breast cancer patients.

EQ-5D bolt-ons for vision, hearing, sleep, fatigue/energy, and social relationships demonstrate added psychometric value in specific populations, but evidence gaps remain in qualitative development, test-retest reliability, responsiveness, differential item functioning, and valuation.
Development of a crosswalk dataset between EQ-5D-Y-5L and EQ-5D-Y-3L to enable rapid value set generation following official instrument launch.
COVID-19 pandemic experiences had statistically significant but complex associations with EQ-5D-5L health state valuations, with different pandemic aspects producing different effects on VAS ratings.
To assess reliability and validity of the UK English version of EQ-5D-Y-5L in children and adolescents aged 8-15 years in South Africa, addressing ceiling effects of the three-level version.
Dissemination of validation findings for the adapted EQ-5D-Y instrument in pediatric populations.
Conversational analysis identified 20 positive and 14 negative interview patterns in EQ-VT interviews that can inform training and quality control procedures across valuation studies.

This study aims to collect Australian EQ-5D-5L preference data using the EQ-VT protocol and compare valuation methods (cTTO and DCE) with online DCETTO to inform methodological development and value set generation.

Approximately 47% of respondents showed comprehension issues with EQ-5D wording, particularly with high-register terms, mid-level severity qualifiers, and dual constructs within dimensions, indicating need for wording improvements to enhance cross-cultural comparability.
To investigate differences in EQ-5D-5L health state preferences between general population and patient samples with chronic lung disease to inform German health care reimbursement decision-making.

EQ-5D-5L was sensitive to capture HRQoL changes over time during the COVID-19 pandemic and revealed significant health burden in younger populations, with over 1 million lives lost in the US youth population.
To assess whether EQ-5D-5L is more sensitive than EQ-5D-3L in predicting productivity loss (absenteeism and presenteeism) across different occupational types.
Large language models can feasibly identify EQ-5D bolt-on dimensions from patient free-text data with substantial agreement to qualitative approaches and generate suitable bolt-on item wordings.

age_group: 0-18 years (self-report: 8-18 years, n=49; caregiver-report: 0-18 years, n=90)
key_finding: EQ-5D-Y-5L and EQ-5D-Y-3L demonstrated promising reliability and responsiveness in children with cystic fibrosis, with EQ-5D-Y-5L showing better patient-caregiver agreement at dimension level than EQ-5D-Y-3L.

This study explores how socioeconomically disadvantaged populations in rural China understand and interpret EQ-5D to identify potential barriers to appropriate use of the instrument in this population.

This study aims to establish prediction models for mapping EQ-5D-5L onto EQ-5D-Y-5L in orthopaedic paediatric patients to enable conversion of previously captured adult-form HRQoL data to the child-appropriate form.

This longitudinal study aims to validate the EQ-5D-5L's ability to detect monthly changes in health-related quality of life from early pregnancy through postpartum and assess its responsiveness and predictive capacity for health changes in pregnant populations.

Knowledge translation project aimed at synthesizing and disseminating guidance on EQ-5D implementation as a PROM for routine outcome measurement in health systems to support decision-making at multiple levels.
A hybrid model combining DCE and cTTO data was used to establish the EQ-5D-Y value set for China, with findings suggesting that cTTO data alone may be sufficient for value set estimation.
statistical_methods: mixed logit model with correlated coefficients

key_finding: This project will explore the psychometric properties (feasibility, reliability, validity, responsiveness) of the EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L among children and adolescents with acute and chronic conditions in Bangladesh using cross-sectional and longitudinal designs.
statistical_methods: variation analysis across dimensions and disease groups

key_finding: The EQ-5D-Y Proxy version 1 requires validity and reliability testing in young children aged 4-8 years, as previous studies suggest certain domains may not be suitable for children under 5-6 years.

Modified composite TTO and DCE valuation methods are feasible and applicable to EQ-HWB-S health and wellbeing states, with DCE preferred over TTO and 'coping' item requiring replacement with 'control'.
Testing psychometric performance of candidate items for the EQALY measure.

This study compares preference structures and measurement properties between DCE and TTO valuation methods across published EQ-5D-5L value sets to identify regional differences and ensure standardized comparability.
To assess the impact of COVID-19 on population health over time across three countries with different lockdown policies using repeated EQ-5D-5L surveys.

Frequency scales demonstrated superior informativity compared to severity scales for pain and discomfort assessment in the EQ-HWB, with differential performance patterns across health conditions suggesting condition-specific measurement optimization opportunities.
The root likelihood (RLH) statistical test is a more reliable alternative to dominant and repeated choice task screening tests for detecting invalid DCE responses.
Self-administered TTO (sTTO) for EQ-5D-5L valuation is more time-efficient than conventional TTO but produces lower data quality with higher logical inconsistencies and inferior modeling performance.

age_group: children and general population aged 15 and above
key_finding: Evaluation of measurement properties of proxy-reported EQ-5D-Y versions in pediatric asthma and eczema, and comparison of psychometric properties of EQ-5D-5L with different recall periods in general population.

age_group: 25-79 years (EQ-DAPHNIE study); not specified for Tromsø and MIC studies
key_finding: Among individuals with identical EQ-5D-5L profiles, educational attainment and income status are systematically associated with higher EQ-VAS scores, suggesting the EQ-5D-5L descriptive system underestimates socioeconomic health inequalities.

age_group: pregnant women and recently delivering women
key_finding: Investigation of mutual cross-sectional and longitudinal relationships between PROMs (EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS) and PREMs (Picker, ReproQ-8D) in antenatal and postnatal care to determine dependency, carry-over effects, and the role of case-mix adjustment in quality of care monitoring.

Different EQ-5D value sets (5L, crosswalk-derived 3L, and mapping-derived 3L) produce substantially different cost-effectiveness results, with mapping-derived values generating notably higher ICERs and potentially different health technology assessment decisions.

The EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S demonstrated good face and content validity across patients, informal carers, and general public members in Italy, with all participants finding the instruments easy to understand and relevant.

EQ-TIPS, EQ-5D-Y-3L, EQ-HWB-S, and EQ-5D-5L demonstrated good reliability, validity, and responsiveness for assessing health outcomes in children with COVID-19 and their parents, with potential for estimating spillover effects.

An interactive online person trade-off survey tool based on cTTO design was developed and demonstrated feasibility and acceptability in phase-1 testing with laypersons for valuing child versus adult QALYs.
A Georgian value set for EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L was developed using cTTO and DCE methods, with mobility and pain/discomfort dimensions showing the largest disutility impacts.

age_group: stratified by age according to Australian Bureau of Statistics data
key_finding: cTTO values obtained from face-to-face and online videoconference interviews are statistically equivalent for mild health states with no significant difference in data quality between modes.

Dissemination and outreach workshop and video tutorial were developed to promote the Italian EQ-5D-5L value set among diverse stakeholder groups including clinical associations, patient advocacy groups, and healthcare organizations.

age_group: adolescents and adults; valuations for a 10-year-old child
key_finding: Adolescents and adults experience doubt and reluctance when valuing children's health states, but the study demonstrates the feasibility of including adolescents in valuation studies and provides insights into cognitive processes during health state valuation.

This mixed-methods study aims to assess health-related quality of life measurement properties of EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in Ethiopian adolescents and establish population norms while exploring content validity and acceptability in adolescents with type 1 diabetes.
A stakeholder engagement meeting to communicate EQ-5D instrument developments and potential applications to Asian HTA agencies and health policy makers.

High-quality evidence supports sufficient construct validity for EQ-5D-Y and most other generic preference-weighted measures in children and adolescents, but evidence for test-retest reliability and responsiveness is limited.
A robust EQ-5D-5L value set was developed for Slovenia with values ranging from -1.09 to 1, showing logical consistency and greater disutility in pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression dimensions.
The first EuroQol Latin American Academy Meeting was convened to bring together researchers and stakeholders from the Latin American region to advance EuroQol research and applications.

Using at least 20 health states evenly distributed across the scale in DCE-to-TTO mapping studies improves predictive precision, and non-linear hybrid models can further enhance precision in populations showing departures from linearity.

A nationally representative EQ-5D-5L value set for Pakistan was successfully developed using hybrid heteroskedastic Tobit modeling of cTTO and DCE data, with utility values ranging from 1.000 (full health) to -0.669 (worst health state).

Cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation of EQ-5D-Y instruments into Chichewa revealed that health-related concepts are complex to translate and that the EQ-5D-Y-5L was less efficient than the EQ-5D-Y at detecting differences in health status in a Malawian pediatric population.

age_group: adolescents (self-valuation) and adults (valuing child health states)
key_finding: This project will develop value sets for the EQ-5D-Y-3L in Germany, Spain and Slovenia by comparing health state preferences between adolescents and adults using DCE anchored with TTO data.
Development of EQ-5D-5L value set for Uganda using composite TTO with 500 participants, and evaluation of a 'lite' valuation protocol to guide future studies in low and middle-income countries.
Workshop designed to enhance technical capacity of early career researchers in estimating EQ-5D value sets using choice data and latent class analysis methods.

instruments: bolt-on: physical activities due to shortness of breath
key_finding: Adding respiratory bolt-ons to the EQ-5D-5L improved descriptive sensitivity in people with respiratory conditions, with the breathing problems bolt-on showing greater independence from other dimensions than the physical activity limitation bolt-on.

Psychometric testing of E-QALY candidate items in Germany identified item performance characteristics to inform selection for a longer profile measure and short classifier, with most items showing good discrimination between health groups but some differential item functioning concerns.
Adolescents contributed weaker preferences than adults in DCE valuation, with older adolescents (14-17) showing better data quality; pain/discomfort was the most important dimension for US youth.
A new TTO variant was developed that better measures worse-than-dead EQ-5D health states compared to composite TTO by mitigating floor effects in negative values.

An updated EQ-5D-5L value set for China was estimated using a more representative population sample and hybrid cTTO-DCE methods, showing significant differences from the original value set reflecting evolving health preferences.

Variation in self-reported health measured by EQ-5D-5L is predominantly explained by patient-level factors (99.57%) rather than general practice or health system characteristics, with some explanatory factors showing condition-specific effects.

EQ-5D was the most widely used generic preference-based measure in East and South-East Asia with sufficient construct validity and responsiveness, and demonstrated important role in cost-utility analyses across Asian populations.

HTA practitioners globally most frequently use EQ-5D for utility measurement, prefer TTO and VAS elicitation methods, and identify key research priorities including developing instruments to capture healthcare/social care and carer impacts.

Interactions between EQ-5D-5L core dimensions and bolt-ons are complex and influenced by presentation order, with cognition and vision generating the most shifts in perceived importance depending on valuation sequence.
Comparison of agreement and psychometric properties between self-complete, interviewer-administered, and proxy-report modes of the Amharic EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in children and adolescents.
Exploratory visit to establish collaborative opportunities for routine PROM data collection and EQ-related research integration within the New Zealand healthcare system.

Development of culturally adapted Argentinean Spanish versions of the EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S instruments through translation, back-translation, and cognitive interviewing to ensure accuracy and cultural relevance.

The EQ-HWB-S demonstrates similar psychometric performance and strong convergent validity across culturally and linguistically diverse and non-diverse Australian populations, supporting its use as an outcome measure in diverse population groups.

Development of adaptive D-efficient DCE methods with sign and monotonicity constraints to estimate individualized preference functions for the EQ-5D-5L with internal validation through preference reflection.
Non-parametric models using country-specific bandwidth optimization improved goodness of fit compared to standard parametric models for EQ-5D-5L value set generation across eight countries.

Qualitative investigation to identify quality of life domains important to people with cognitive or visual impairment beyond current EQ-5D coverage to inform bolt-on development and validate content and construct validity.
DCETTO approach and choice set construction method impact value sets differently across countries, with efficient DCE designs showing slightly better performance but requiring priors.

A national value set for the EQ-5D-Y-3L was developed for Hungary based on adult preferences, with pain/discomfort being the most important domain and 12.8% of health states having negative utilities.
statistical_methods: mixed logit model with random-correlated coefficients

key_finding: Health preferences of the Danish general population remained stable between 2019 and 2024 despite major societal challenges including the COVID-19 pandemic and war in Europe, suggesting EQ-5D-5L value sets do not require re-estimation.

Video and in-person TTO interviews for EQ-5D-5L valuation are both feasible and acceptable with similar utility values, though mode may affect sample representativeness across demographic characteristics.

An advisory committee meeting educated end-users and stakeholders on EQ-5D and PROMs use, identified implementation research questions in primary care, and expanded the network of EQ-5D users across Alberta and Canada.

An EQ-5D-5L value set representing the preferences of patients with heart disease was developed using composite time trade-off valuation, with utility values ranging from -0.727 to 1.0 and demonstrating good discriminative ability across functional classes.

Respondents identified health and quality of life aspects including relationships, activities, and social dimensions that appear more frequently in quality of life than health descriptions, with notable differences between UK and Australian populations.

A novel method using direct observations from neighbouring EQ-5D-5L health states averaged with econometric model predictions can improve value set construction and mitigate non-monotonicity issues in preference data.

This project aims to systematically review EQ-5D population norms literature, develop comprehensive guidelines for their development and reporting, and create an interactive website for accessing norm data to enhance reliability and usability.
Indonesia EQ-5D-5L value set and population norm scores were published to support health technology assessment and reimbursement decisions in the Indonesian health insurance system.
The EQ-5D was the most widely used utility-based instrument in cost-utility analyses of cancer treatments, accounting for 27.9% of original utility data and 24.3% of cited utilities.

Patients with prior coronary artery bypass graft surgery had significantly worse quality of life outcomes at 30 days following percutaneous coronary intervention compared to those without prior surgery.

The EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-9 instruments were successfully translated into Dutch following standardized EuroQol translation guidelines including forward translation, backward translation, and cognitive debriefing.

Workshop to educate health technology assessment stakeholders in China on approaches to valuing health outcomes using patient-reported measures, with EQ-5D featured as a leading global utility instrument.

This project aims to determine whether EQ-5D data can capture the negative effects of adverse drug reactions on patient quality of life for use in quantitative benefit-risk assessment of pharmaceuticals.
Dissemination of findings on psychometric validation of EQ-5D-Y instruments and health state valuation at ISPOR 2024 Conference.
Revision and enhancement of a patient decision aid for total knee arthroplasty with improved EQ-5D data visualization and inclusion of patient preference items regarding wait time and symptom levels.

Machine learning cluster analysis can identify preference heterogeneity in composite TTO data, revealing distinct respondent groups with different scale use patterns and domain preferences that may be hidden in aggregate analyses.
Development of software tools (Stata, R, Excel) for calculating EQ-5D utility values and analyzing EQ-5D data with integrated published value sets and crosswalk functionality.
Workshop presentation on the development, current applications, and future directions of the EQ-5D-5L instrument.
Episodic Future Thinking does not significantly reduce time preference distortion in composite TTO valuation of EQ-5D-5L health states.

The EQ-5D-Y-3L instrument successfully identified groups of Ethiopian adolescents with lower health-related quality of life and demonstrated feasibility and usefulness in a low-middle income country setting.
The EQ-5D-5L demonstrates better psychometric properties than the EQ-5D-3L for measuring health-related quality of life in Chinese patients with Pompe disease.

The EQ-HWB's conceptual framework is well-represented in Chinese QoL frameworks, with a newly identified 'mindset' domain reflecting cultural characteristics, though some items require clarification for cultural and linguistic appropriateness.

The EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S demonstrated excellent psychometric properties including test-retest reliability, convergent validity, and known-group validity across literate, illiterate, and patient populations in Indonesia.

The EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrated feasibility and comparable psychometric performance to the EQ-5D-Y-3L among adolescents living with HIV in South Africa, with better discriminatory power in certain dimensions.

age_group: adults rating health states of children (4-year-old, 10-year-old, unspecified age) and other adults
key_finding: Preferences for EQ-5D-Y-3L health states differ significantly by perspective (child vs. adult), with dimension importance and value set scale varying between perspectives, and DCE producing more varied results than the OPUF tool.

A systematic literature review and bibliographic database of >60 studies were developed to identify key conceptual questions regarding bolt-on development, nomenclature, definitions, and appropriate use circumstances for EQ-5D bolt-ons.

This study explores how healthcare professionals in community settings use EQ-5D data to support clinical decision-making and identifies barriers, facilitators, and training needs for improved integration into clinical workflows.

age_group: 1 month to 18 years (66 children aged 1 month to 4 years, 78 children aged 5-18 years)
key_finding: EQ-TIPS, Y-3L and Y-5L demonstrated superior psychometric performance compared to PedsQL and PTHSI in children dependent on technology for breathing, with proxy versions showing better performance than self-report versions.

The UK public demonstrates greater willingness to prioritize health interventions for poorer populations when gains involve life-expectancy compared to quality-of-life improvements across EQ-5D domains.

This study aims to improve EQ-VT TTO data quality by testing alternative routing procedures (randomized routing and non-stopping TTO) to reduce response spikes, logical inconsistencies, and satisficing bias.
Development of a Swedish EQ-5D-5L value set using composite TTO and DCE methods with a nationally representative sample.
statistical_methods: hybrid model combining TTO and DCE data

key_finding: This study explores whether time preferences and lexicographic preferences for immediate death explain differences between EQ-5D-Y utilities elicited from proxy versus individual perspectives.

age_group: adults valuing health states from both adult and 10-year-old child perspectives
key_finding: Heuristic valuation processes are more prevalent in EQ-5D valuation from a child perspective compared to adult perspective, with evidence of lower data quality and clustering of utilities in child perspectives.

A multilevel conceptual framework was developed to explain higher ceiling effects in EQ-5D instruments among Asian populations compared to Western populations, incorporating cultural, structural, measurement, and data collection factors.

A multivariate regression framework for case-mix adjustment of EQ-5D profiles can improve hospital performance assessment by preserving dimension-specific information and reducing value set dependency.
Generate a Philippine-specific EQ-5D-5L value set to standardize health technology assessments and QALY calculations for pharmaceutical policy decisions.

Health-related quality of life in China is conceptualized through two frameworks—one based on Traditional Chinese Medicine theory (Yin-Yang balance) and another aligned with WHO health definition—with partial overlap but distinct concepts including environmental adaptability, emotional experiences, and cognitive function not fully captured by EQ-5D.
Development of the first Chinese value set for EQ-5D-Y while exploring age dependency and latent variable effects on time trade-off ratios across different age groups.

EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrates slightly lower ceiling effects and higher responsiveness to health improvement compared to EQ-5D-Y-3L, while both instruments show comparable discriminative ability, convergent validity, and test-retest reliability in pediatric patients with heart diseases.

The EQ-5D-Y was successfully cross-culturally adapted for Singapore with minor modifications, and the descriptive system was found to be relevant and comprehensive for measuring poor health in local children, though bolt-on dimensions for social relationships and appetite may be beneficial.
Comparative evaluation of 11 inequality measures applied to EQ-5D-3L data reveals inconsistencies in outcomes and performance across different theoretical bases and underlying assumptions.

DCE with duration can produce similar value sets to cTTO when nonlinear time preferences are accounted for and anchoring is based on duration, enabling EQ-5D-5L valuation in resource-limited settings.
statistical_methods: hybrid model combining cTTO and DCE data

key_finding: The Amharic EQ-5D-Y-5L Experimental version demonstrates good reliability and known group validity for assessing health-related quality of life in children with prevalent disease conditions in Ethiopia.

This program develops comprehensive EuroQol guidance for testing psychometric properties of generic preference-based instruments through critical literature review, empirical comparison of quantitative methods, and consensus-based recommendations.
Both EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L demonstrate sufficient construct validity and convergent validity for assessing health-related quality of life in patients with hematological cancers.

age_group: 15+ years, with specific focus on 15-17 year olds (355 UK, 363 Swedish) and general public adults
key_finding: Most UK and Swedish respondents thought older children and adolescents should be involved in valuing child and adolescent health and that trading off life years would be acceptable for them.
Health state fluctuations occur frequently in dementia and are associated with higher EQ-5D-5L health utility changes and non-adherence to the instrument's recall period of today.

EQ-5D-5L demonstrated construct validity, test-retest reliability, and responsiveness to worsened health status in patients with Graves' disease, though responsiveness to health improvement requires further investigation.

age_group: general population, tended to be older
key_finding: PAPRIKA was successfully used to value EQ-HWB-S with feasibility demonstrated through participant feedback and utility weights similar to EQ-PVT, though with some dimensional weight differences potentially reflecting reduced attribute non-attendance.

A pilot study exploring the conceptual basis, methodological approaches, and feasibility of developing deep-dive modules for the EQ-5D-5L to provide more granular measurement of health-related quality of life within each dimension.

The EQ-5D-5L with respiratory bolt-ons improved psychometric properties by reducing ceiling effects and increasing informativity, though important concepts like fatigue, sleep, and social relations remain uncaptured.
The EQ-HWB-S demonstrated good validity, responsiveness to change, feasibility and acceptability in caregivers of children experiencing adversity.

Respiratory bolt-ons, particularly the symptoms dimension (R2), enhanced the psychometric properties of EQ-5D-5L in obstructive airway disease patients by reducing ceiling effects and improving construct validity and responsiveness.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, approximately one-third of respondents showed improved or deteriorated health-related quality of life, with negative life events having larger effects than positive events, and insufficient healthcare access associated with greater HRQoL variability.

A Ghanaian EQ-5D-5L value set was successfully developed using cTTO and DCE data from 300 adults, with a Hybrid Tobit model selected as the preferred preference model for estimating QALYs in health technology assessment.

Weighted rating scale scores (RSW and RSW2) and multidimensional IRT demonstrated superior psychometric properties for patient-reported summary scores of EQ-5D-5L compared to traditional level sum scores and value set-based approaches.

The EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrated superior measurement properties compared to the EQ-5D-Y-3L in Brazilian children and adolescents, with lower ceiling effects and sufficient construct validity when compared to CHU9D, particularly for those with disabling musculoskeletal pain.
EQ-5D utilities and EQ VAS scores were similar between rivaroxaban plus aspirin and aspirin alone groups despite differences in clinical outcomes.

EQ-5D dimensions have differential impacts on health-related quality of life versus broader life satisfaction and subjective well-being measures, with anxiety/depression showing the strongest associations with happiness outcomes.
An Australian value set for the EQ-5D-Y-3L was successfully developed using cTTO and DCE data, enabling QALY calculation for paediatric health economic evaluation.

age_group: mixed ages (purposively sampled by age and gender)
key_finding: Skin irritation and self-confidence bolt-ons are relevant and improve content validity of the EQ-5D-5L in psoriasis patients, with minimal conceptual overlap with existing dimensions.
This study aims to produce the first preference-based national EQ-5D-5L value set for Serbia using EuroQol Valuation Technology protocol combining TTO and DCE methods.
This study develops and validates response mapping approaches between EQ-TIPS-5L and EQ-5D-Y-5L to enable preference-weighting of EQ-TIPS data using EQ-5D-Y value sets in young children.

This study will assess the psychometric performance of EQ-5D-5L with bolt-ons (skin irritation, self-confidence, sleep, and social/relationship difficulties) in Chinese patients with atopic dermatitis to expand evidence on bolt-on validity and responsiveness to Asian populations.

Addition of EQ-5D-5L data to administrative data improves prediction of high-cost healthcare users, particularly for cost capture, with potential to identify individuals who could benefit from targeted interventions.
statistical_methods: area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUROC)

key_finding: This project aims to develop and validate EQ-5D-5L bolt-on descriptors for hearing to improve measurement sensitivity in hearing-related impairment through mixed-methods research across three phases.

Clustering algorithms identified distinct subgroups in Latin American populations based on sociodemographic and EQ-5D response patterns, with cluster membership significantly predicting differences in self-rated health (EQ-VAS) scores.

Differences between own health and child health perspective TTO values are driven by both perspective shift (self vs. other) and age considerations (adult vs. child), but these differences do not appear in VAS data, suggesting they may be technique-specific artifacts.
EQ-5D-5L, EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S demonstrate satisfactory known-groups validity but limited responsiveness in measuring health and wellbeing impact of heatwaves among older adults.
The study compares alternative approaches for anchoring DCE data with cTTO data to produce EQ-5D-Y-3L value sets.

The EQ-5D-Y-5L descriptive system does not present significant problems when presented in DCE valuation tasks, though some minor coefficient inconsistencies were observed across countries and adolescents showed greater response inconsistency than adults.
A PROMs-based decision aid using EQ-5D can improve patient expectations and decision quality for total knee arthroplasty by providing realistic outcome information prior to surgery consultation.

age_group: children and adolescents (EQ-5D-Y) compared with adults (EQ-5D-5L)
key_finding: Comparative analysis of EQ-5D-Y-3L value sets across countries and valuation methods to understand differences in youth versus adult preferences and inform future protocol updates.

Allowing heterogeneity in scale and rate parameters in mixed logit models significantly improves the face validity of EQ-5D-5L value sets by reducing insignificant incremental effects and revealing that scale and rate are highly correlated.

A three-day training workshop successfully prepared 18 interviewers for conducting EQ-5D valuation interviews using time trade-off methodology, with all participants passing quality control assessments.

EQ-5D is a valid instrument for assessing health-related quality of life in elderly populations and can differentiate between frail and non-frail elderly and between users and non-users of social/long-term care.
The EQ-5D-5L demonstrated better content and construct validity than the EQ-5D-3L in patients with advanced melanoma, with lower ceiling effects and superior discriminatory performance.

age_group: adults aged 18 or above valuing health states from a child perspective
key_finding: A Hong Kong-specific EQ-5D-Y-3L value set was developed from adult preferences for child health states, with no significant preference differences between adult own and child perspectives.
statistical_methods: model estimation from DCE and cTTO responses

key_finding: Both EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB-9 demonstrate suitable performance for assessing outcomes among informal carers, though EQ-HWB-9 shows less ceiling effect and captures carer-relevant impairments more comprehensively.
A novel combined instrument approach using EQ-5D-5L and ASCOT was developed to measure and value health and social care outcomes on the same scale.

This study evaluates the psychometric properties of EQ-5D-Y-5L and EQ-HWB-9 in children with cerebral palsy and their caregivers, examining HRQoL profiles and spillover effects on caregiver well-being over six months.
The project aims to improve and introduce new discrete choice experiment methods for health-state valuations within the EuroQol framework.

The Amharic EQ-5D-3L, EQ-5D-5L, EQ-5D-Y-3L, and EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrate comparable psychometric performance with acceptable feasibility, good test-retest reliability, and significant known group validity across healthy adolescents and those with HIV or epilepsy in Ethiopia.
Kaizen tasks were developed and implemented to elicit preference paths for sequential relief of child health problems, with examination of heterogeneity by child age and problem duration.

The position of dead on the health-utility scale has important consequences for decision-making in cost-utility analysis, and ratio scale properties are needed to preserve indifferences in the QALY model.

Negative cTTO values are sensitive to health state severity when analysed at the individual respondent level rather than in isolation, supporting the validity of the cTTO method for worse-than-dead states.

The Afaan-Oromo EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrates improved measurement properties compared to the Y-3L, with reduced ceiling effects, greater discriminatory power, and higher test-retest reliability while maintaining comparable feasibility and known-group validity.
The digital version of EQ-5D-5L in Shona is measurement equivalent to the paper version and is feasible and acceptable for implementation in routine HIV care in a low-resource setting.

Single Profile Preference Elicitation (SPP) is a feasible and acceptable alternative valuation method for bolt-on items with lower cognitive burden and potentially improved precision compared to standard DCE.

age_group: older adults aged 65 and over living in residential aged care facilities
key_finding: This study will assess the psychometric properties, feasibility, and implementation of EQ-HWB-S in residential aged care facilities in Italy, including evaluation of self-reported, interviewer-administered, and proxy-reported administration modes.

Death thought accessibility and attachment style emerge as novel psychological factors influencing VAS and TTO health valuations, with weak but significant associations particularly for self-experienced health measures.
A new UK value set for the EQ-5D-5L was generated using time trade-off preferences from a representative sample of 1200 UK general public participants.

age_group: adolescents (11-17 years) and adults (18 years and older)
key_finding: This study aims to estimate EQ-5D-Y-3L value sets for the United Kingdom using DCE anchored with cTTO, exploring different normative perspectives and sample representativeness scenarios.
Testing whether modifying the TTO protocol (finer granularity and alternative framing) reduces non-trading and all-in-trading corner answers that bias value set estimation.

Project aimed to generate EQ-5D-3L population norms for China and investigate health inequalities across social determinants using National Health Services Survey data from 2008, 2013, and 2018, but was cancelled due to data access restrictions imposed by Chinese regulations on international data sharing.
GHQ-12 can only partially predict EQ-5D-5L responses, suggesting that direct mathematical mapping between these instruments may result in information loss and be conceptually problematic.
Investigation of measurement properties, development of country-specific norms, and analysis of health inequalities and socioeconomic determinants of health in elderly Europeans using EQ-5D-3L.

Systematic review investigating barriers and opportunities for EQ-5D use as a patient-reported outcome measure in quality of care assessment, with specific focus on orthopedic surgery applications across different healthcare systems.
This project investigates the construct validity of (c)TTO methods by examining the role of death as a conceptual determinant of health utility valuations.
To establish contemporary EQ-5D population norms reflecting COVID-19 impacts and use health-related quality of life metrics to inform vaccine prioritization decisions across multiple countries.

The Chichewa versions of both EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrated reliability and validity for use among children and adolescents in Malawi, though the EQ-5D-Y-3L showed superior empirical validity for detecting health status differences.
Interim psychometric testing of EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L in China to identify problematic items and inform international item selection decisions.

The EQ-5D-5L composite anxiety/depression dimension demonstrates good convergent validity with separate anxiety and depression dimensions and clinical symptom measures, with performance varying by age group.

Monotonicity constraints in Bayesian DCE designs may improve efficiency and enable more complex preference modeling with smaller samples in health utility valuation studies without increasing respondent burden.
Adolescents can value both EQ-5D-Y-5L and EQ-5D-5L with similar preference weights across dimensions, and believe their preferences should contribute to social value sets.
A Moroccan EQ-5D-5L value set was successfully developed using a nationally representative sample, with pain/discomfort being the most impactful dimension on health state preferences.

This study tests the psychometric validity of the E-QALY item pool in US cancer patients to assess generalizability of UK findings and support item reduction and selection for a broad quality of life measure for economic evaluations.

This project aims to examine the desirability, feasibility, and impact of involving children aged 8-18 years in the valuation of EQ-5D-Y health states, addressing evidence gaps regarding stakeholder involvement in health preference research.
Task sequence affects response times and rounding behavior in TTO but not paired comparison precision, with learning effects plateauing after the first 3 tasks.
The study examines whether health state preferences differ when 1-year episodes are acute, chronic, or generic, with implications for health technology assessment and future EQ-5D valuation studies.

This study evaluates the psychometric properties of EQ-5D-5L bolt-ons (breathing, sleep, fatigue, self-confidence) and EQ-HWB instruments (EQ-HWB-25 and EQ-HWB-9) to identify more feasible and sensitive patient-reported outcome measures for health-related quality of life monitoring in individuals with obesity receiving weight-loss interventions.

age_group: mixed, with subgroup analysis of age <50 years
key_finding: EQ-5D-3L health utilities in cancer patients are influenced by socioeconomic factors including income and sex, with lower income associated with lower utilities and younger age associated with lower utilities in females but not males.
The partially-fixed model offers a cost-effective approach to valuing EQ-5D bolt-on dimensions across multiple countries.
This study compares the feasibility, psychometric properties, and responsiveness of proxy EQ-5D-5L-Y versus proxy EQ-5D-3L-Y in caregivers of children and adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis.

Fair to moderate agreement was observed between child self-reports and parent proxy reports on the EQ-5D-Y-3L, with agreement varying by age group, gender, and dimension, and both versions demonstrating acceptable convergent validity and responsiveness to health status changes.

The EQ-HWB-9 demonstrates acceptable content validity in Hungarian social care but requires refinements for Slovenian long-term care users, particularly for abstract concepts and complex needs populations.

The TANDI, a new proxy-completed HRQoL measure for infants and toddlers aged 0-3 years based on the EuroQol model, demonstrated good content validity and psychometric properties including internal consistency (α=0.83) and ability to discriminate between children with acute illness, chronic illness, and general population.
Level overlap and color coding in discrete choice experiments independently reduce drop-out rates and improve attribute attendance, with combined use being most effective.

The second African Regional Academy aims to build capacity in health-related quality of life measurement and expand the use of EQ-5D across African countries through researcher networks and methodological training.
An educational workshop on EQ-5D-Y was successfully delivered to Asia-Pacific researchers and clinicians, with online content reaching 229+ users through knowledge-sharing platforms.

Population norms for EQ-5D and VAS in four Latin American countries show higher health-related quality of life in Argentina and Uruguay compared to Brazil and Chile, with values declining with age and lower in females across all countries.
End-user conference and Scientific Advisory Committee meeting to discuss EQ-5D research directions and establish APERSU research agenda for Alberta.

The EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrate good acceptability and content validity among adolescents with Type 1 diabetes in Ethiopia, though diabetes-specific and social aspects of health are not captured within the instruments.

The EQ-5D-Y demonstrates content validity in assessing HRQoL in children and adolescents with chronic conditions, with health complaints and mental health problems significantly predicting quality of life outcomes.
Develop a Nigeria-specific QALY value set for youth using EQ-5D-Y-3L with hybrid cTTO and DCE methods to enable valid cost-effectiveness analyses in the Nigerian healthcare context.
Health and social care aspects of quality of life can be valued jointly on the same underlying scale using discrete choice experiments, with evidence of preference heterogeneity across dimensions.

EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S demonstrated construct validity for assessing caregiver health and well-being, and care recipient proxy assessments offer a novel approach for capturing caregiver spillover effects in economic evaluations.

Implausible health states are common in EQ-5D-5L valuation studies but should be retained in modelling as their exclusion increases prediction error, despite respondents finding them difficult to value.

Adjusted Population Attributable Risk calculation is a valuable analytical technique for analyzing health inequalities in EQ-5D scores, with strong relationships found between hospitals and socioeconomic status in regional anesthesia use and effectiveness for hip and knee arthroplasty.

Patient-derived EQ-5D value sets produce different hospital performance rankings and outlier classifications compared to general population weights, with latent class analysis revealing heterogeneous patient preferences associated with observable characteristics.

Multidimensional item response theory models with reinforcing items from other patient-reported outcome measures provide a feasible approach to psychometric evaluation of the EQ-5D-5L, with parameter stability dependent on sufficient item coverage reflecting EQ-5D-5L content breadth.
statistical_methods: item response theory parameter stability assessment

key_finding: EQ-PSO and EQ-PSO+sleep demonstrated improved psychometric performance over EQ-5D-5L in atopic dermatitis patients, particularly in capturing symptom severity and quality of life impairments.
The Better than Dead method is feasible and reliable for valuing EQ-5D-5L health states, with time-dependent preferences influenced by religious beliefs and education level.

Health state selection criteria and sampling ratio critically influence misspecification of value functions in EQ-5D tariff estimation, with sampling ratios below 1:10 being hazardous and interaction models increasing misspecification when applied to incomplete datasets.

This PhD project will assess the psychometric performance of EQ-5D-5L bolt-on items and explore the psychometric properties of EQ-HWB-S and its relationship with other health and well-being instruments across multiple countries using longitudinal POPCORN study data.

EuroQol Group has developed multiple TTO valuation protocols (MVH, Paris, EQ-VT) with varying methodological approaches for valuing EQ-5D health states to support QALY calculations in health technology assessment.

Adding four sleep-related bolt-ons to EQ-5D-5L improved psychometric properties including reduced ceiling effects and enhanced construct validity, responsiveness, and discriminatory power in patients with sleep disturbances.

Presenting health states 'in context' of the full EQ-5D-5L descriptive system significantly reduces logically dominated responses and produces larger preference decrements between severity levels, particularly for levels 4 and 5.

age_group: health care workers and medical workers
key_finding: This study evaluates the psychometric performance of an extended EQ-5D-5L with cognition and social participation bolt-ons in German health care workers with COVID-19 infection to assess suitability for infectious disease populations.
A feedback module and separation of better-than-dead and worse-than-dead tasks improved data consistency in EQ-5D-5L valuation, with differential effects by country.

age_group: older people in aged care settings
key_finding: The project unravelled the self-report versus proxy-assessment conundrum by examining how cognitive impairment and dementia affect self-assessed HRQoL in older people using EQ-5D-5L, and assessed inter-rater agreement across different proxy perspectives.
Testing whether multiplicative models are superior to additive models for exploring the effect of bolt-on/off items on EQ-5D health state valuation.

age_group: 18 years and above (with stakeholder consultation including discussion of adolescents aged 11+)
key_finding: Pakistan's first nationally representative EQ-5D-Y-3L value set was successfully developed using DCE and cTTO methods with 2,000 respondents from six major cities, with pain/discomfort identified as the dimension with greatest influence on preference values.

Clinical quality of primary care as measured by QOF indicators shows statistically significant positive associations with patient self-reported health on EQ-5D-5L in cross-sectional analyses, but these effects become non-significant when accounting for unobserved time-invariant practice characteristics.
The composite time trade-off method appears largely insensitive to severity for health states worse than dead, and the threshold explanation does not adequately explain this insensitivity.

Examine how health-related quality of life preferences vary systematically according to chronic disease status and comorbidity patterns in a representative New Zealand population using personal value sets.

Quality-adjusted life expectancy gaps between major cities and remote/very remote areas in Australia are wider than life expectancy gaps alone, with intersectional differences in utility values observed.

Expansion of composite time trade-off states from 10 to 23 in EQ-5D-Y-3L valuation protocol reveals non-linearity in health state values, particularly for worst health states, supporting the use of non-linear mapping models in value set generation.
Workshop and issue panel conducted at ISPOR Asia-Pacific Conference to engage the health outcomes research community.

This study evaluates the appropriateness of the 7-day recall period for the proxy version of the EQ-HWB in dementia carers and addresses a critical gap in understanding recall period selection for proxy-reported health measures.

The EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S instruments demonstrated valid and reliable measurement properties in parents of children with health conditions, with good discrimination between caregiver groups and support for relevance, comprehensibility, and comprehensiveness.

An EQ-5D-5L value set was successfully established for the Ethiopian general population using composite time trade-off and discrete choice experiments, with anxiety/depression showing the greatest impact on utility decrement.
Zermelo-Bradley-Terry models produced better fit to discrete choice experiment data and fewer inconsistencies compared to logit models in EQ-5D-5L valuation across seven countries.

A respiratory bolt-on dimension for the EQ-5D-5L focusing on shortness of breath impact on physical activities and respiratory symptoms was developed and identified as a candidate for valuation studies to improve responsiveness in asthma and COPD patients.
A US EQ-5D-5L value set was derived using a hybrid cTTO/DCE model with values ranging from -0.699 to 1.0, with 23.5% of health states valued as worse-than-dead.

To produce an EQ-5D-Y-3L value set for Poland based on general adult population preferences and explore modifications to the cTTO protocol to improve discriminatory power and face validity of negative utilities.
This study aims to characterize regional variation in COVID-19's impact on quality of life in the U.S. as a function of region-specific social isolation control policies.
Development and application of improved EQ-5D-5L valuation protocol 2.0 using composite time trade-off in Germany to generate a German tariff for the EQ-5D-5L.
Three new methods (HSDI, HSDC, and PLFs) can characterize the distribution of EQ-5D health profiles and provide insights into patient health clustering and differences between EQ-5D versions.
Translation and cognitive debriefing of Dutch version of EQ-5D vision bolt-ons to ensure clarity, naturalness, and adequate interpretation for future validation or valuation work.

Both EQ-5D-5L and AQoL-8D demonstrated validity as generic preference-based measures for use in informal carer populations based on convergent validity, known-groups validity, ceiling effects, and test-retest reliability.

Adding four bolt-ons (skin irritation, self-confidence, social relationships, and sleep) to the EQ-5D-5L improved psychometric performance in patients with psoriasis and atopic dermatitis, particularly reducing ceiling effects and enhancing responsiveness to health changes.
This study will assess health-related quality of life in pregnant and postpartum women during the COVID-19 pandemic to document maternal health impacts and healthcare needs.
Demographic change in age and gender composition does not significantly contribute to EQ-5D-3L value set obsolescence.

This qualitative study investigates the feasibility of applying DCE latent scale methodology to EQ-TIPS-5L valuation by examining how caregivers and general public respondents interpret dimensions and engage with choice tasks.

Health and lifestyle-related attitudes explain significant differences in self-rated health and life-satisfaction, with unconfident fatalists showing the poorest health perceptions and life-satisfaction outcomes.

age_group: children under 8 years with emphasis on younger age group
key_finding: This study aims to validate self-complete, interviewer-administered, and proxy-administered versions of EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in Chinese children with high disease burden across multiple paediatric conditions.

Adding a cognitive dimension to the EQ-5D-3L increases explanatory power for health-related quality of life in injury patients, with cognitive problems showing comparable impact to other EQ-5D dimensions.
Canadian stakeholders predominantly support direct preference elicitation from adolescents using DCE methodology for EQ-5D-Y valuation, with preference for the 5-level over 3-level version.

This conceptual research project aims to address key methodological and normative questions in the valuation of health states in children, including whose preferences should be elicited, whose health should be valued, and which valuation methods are most appropriate.

Linear mixed models perform slightly better than multiple imputation strategies for handling missing EQ-5D-5L data in clinical trials, with index-level imputation preferred over response-level imputation.

This study examines the impact of COVID-19 on health-related quality of life in adults visiting emergency departments and primary care clinics in Alberta, identifying disproportionate effects across population subgroups.

cTTO and DCE methods were feasible for deriving EQ-HWB-S utilities in the UK general population, with pain, mobility, and daily activities showing the largest disutilities, though public stakeholders raised concerns about sample diversity and representativeness.
Assessment of the validity and responsiveness of EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB to capture the health impact of heatwaves in older adults.

Item selection methods for generic descriptive system development vary considerably across studies, with most using empirical statistical approaches (regression, factor analysis, or IRT) rather than relying solely on content validity.
EQ-5D-5L has achieved strong institutional adoption across Asian HTA agencies, but significant implementation gaps prevent optimal utilisation.
A workshop was delivered to 55 healthcare professionals in Singapore on implementing EQ-5D as a PROM to improve clinical decision-making and patient-centered care in routine practice.

A new generic measure (EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S) was developed to assess the impact of health and social care interventions on service users and informal carers, extending beyond traditional health-related quality of life.
Non-linear time preference specifications in DCE models produce utility estimates on a similar scale to TTO with better model fit and predictive validity than constant proportionality approaches.

The E-QALY project developed a broad generic preference-based measure of quality of life for use across health care, social care and public health through five stages of domain identification, item generation, face validity testing, psychometric testing, and valuation across six countries.
Development of a centralised compendium of EQ-5D-5L value sets and valuation studies to serve as an accessible resource for users, updating the previous Szende et al. (2007) compendium for EQ-5D-3L.

This study explores interpretation difficulties in the EQ-5D-5L Pain/Discomfort dimension, particularly regarding wording of response options and differential interpretation between people with physical versus mental health conditions.

age_group: mixed, with subgroup analysis by age
key_finding: COVID-19 patients showed reduced health-related quality of life with pooled EQ-5D utility score of 0.79, with pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression as most affected dimensions.
Comparison of responsiveness of EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L index scores to health improvement from cataract surgery, and evaluation of whether a vision bolt-on item improves responsiveness.

A capacity-building workshop to increase utilization of EQ-5D as a patient-reported outcome measure across African countries and establish researcher networks for methodological research and valuation studies.
This study aims to develop and recommend an optimal mapping function between EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L to enable derivation of health utilities from Y-5L data using available Y-3L value sets.
Investigation of methodological approaches to constructing EQ-5D-5L value sets through censoring of time-trade-off data at zero.
The EQ-5D-5L Hausa version demonstrates valid and reliable psychometric properties for measuring health status in hip replacement patients.

This study aims to establish US population norms for EQ-5D-5L visual analogue and index-based scores stratified by gender, age, and race/ethnicity to facilitate clinical assessment and cost-utility analyses.

Pre-congress session at IHEA Congress in Cape Town focused on EQ-5D as a measure of population health, featuring EuroQol-funded research projects (POPQOL, DAPHNIE, IndiQol) and supporting early career researcher participation from low- and middle-income countries.
The EQ-HWB-9 demonstrates strong psychometric properties and validity for assessing health and wellbeing in the UK general population.

The Arabic version of EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrated superior psychometric properties compared to EQ-5D-Y-3L with reduced ceiling effects, better feasibility, and strong validity and reliability in Egyptian children with and without chronic health conditions.

This study investigates whether the same EQ-5D health state is valued differently across patient groups with different underlying conditions and explores alternative ways of summarizing EQ-5D data using experience-based preferences.

age_group: youth 8-15 years old (valued by adults aged 18+ years)
key_finding: This study will estimate the first EQ-5D-Y-3L value set for Saudi Arabia using DCE and cTTO methods to anchor preferences onto the 0-1 QALY scale.
To pilot the inclusion of a VAS response box in EQ-5D-Y versions and examine comprehension of the VAS among younger children aged 8-10 years.
A Polish EQ-5D-5L value set was developed using hybrid cTTO and DCE data, showing greater sensitivity to mild health worsening while maintaining consistency with existing value sets.

Worry about global threats was consistently associated with lower health-related quality of life, while resilience and social connectedness provided protective effects; longitudinal HRQoL trajectories remained largely stable over three years with older age and chronic disease as strong predictors of poorer health states.
Both EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L demonstrate good feasibility properties in elderly populations with acceptably low missing values and completion rates, though slightly higher than in younger age groups.

This project tests whether TTO utilities from EQ-5D and EQ-5D-Y correspond to priority-setting decisions in healthcare allocation between adults and children, and whether VAS weights can replicate this correspondence.

Youth versions (Y-3L and Y-5L) demonstrated more severe health state reporting and higher discriminatory power compared to corresponding adult descriptive systems, with notable differences in pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression dimensions.
This study examines whether different formats and locations of recall period presentation improve respondents' use of recall periods in the EQ-5D-5L among patients with fluctuating conditions.
Sequential stochastic dominance provides an ethically grounded method for comparing population health distributions across countries that reveals differences obscured by summary measures.

This study aims to test the psychometric validity of the E-QALY item pool in Australian respondents to support item reduction and selection for a broad quality of life measure for economic evaluation.
To develop and evaluate a garbage class MIXL model implementation in Stata for identifying random response patterns in discrete choice experiments used for health state valuation.
To compare the sensitivity and discriminative ability of EQ-5D-5L versus EQ-5D-3L descriptive systems and value sets in patients with ischemic heart disease.

A crowdsourced competition identified analytical approaches and model specifications that better predict health preferences in discrete choice experiments, with the winning team achieving superior predictive validity using a two sub-model approach.

This study aims to develop and test four- or five-level versions of the EQ-5D-Y with appropriate severity labels that are comprehensible and feasible for children and adolescents aged 8-15 across six countries.
The five-level versions of EQ-TIPS and EQ-5D-Y demonstrate similar or superior psychometric performance compared to their three-level counterparts in children with severe health conditions.

Eye tracking is a feasible method to study attention patterns and information processing in discrete choice tasks for health-state valuation, revealing that respondents show differential fixation patterns across health-state descriptions.

Adult preferences for valuing child health states vary significantly by perspective and health profile, with own-perspective valuations recommended to minimize methodological bias in child health state valuation.
Varying choice set sizes in DCEs may improve respondent engagement and perceived ease, though effects differ depending on the nature of the choice options being valued.
A comprehensive international review of routine PROM data collection systems to identify knowledge gaps and research opportunities for promoting EQ instruments in health system implementation.
Investigation of health status of Chinese populations during COVID-19 pandemic using EQ-5D-5L to demonstrate the instrument's usefulness in describing health status during a global health crisis.
The Afrikaans version of the EQ-TANDI is well understood, accepted by caregivers, and demonstrates valid measurement properties for children aged 0-36 months in South Africa.
This research investigates regional differences in health-related quality of life as measured by EQ-5D across England over a 20-year period using national survey data.

This qualitative study evaluates the content validity and acceptability of the EQ-5D-5L respiratory bolt-on in asthma patients in Kazakhstan using concept elicitation and cognitive debriefing methods.

SUD patients reported substantially worse health-related quality of life on EQ-5D-3L compared to general population, with anxiety/depression, pain/discomfort, and usual activities as most frequently reported problem domains.

EQ-5D-5L index distributions demonstrate clustering in patient populations, with clustering driven by value set construction rather than profile data alone, highlighting the need for careful exploratory data analysis in statistical testing.

Preferences elicited through DCEs and TTO tasks show association across EQ-5D-5L dimensions but poor agreement at the individual health state level, indicating that value set development should use methods requiring association but not agreement when combining both techniques.

age_group: adults valuing health states for a 10-year-old child or themselves
key_finding: This study investigates whether respondent characteristics (e.g., having children, life expectancies, time preference, loss aversion) bias TTO valuation of EQ-5D-Y differently when adults value health states for themselves versus for a hypothetical 10-year-old child, and tests feasibility of correcting for these biases.
Proxy-reported EQ-5D-Y-3L demonstrates good feasibility and satisfactory agreement with patient self-report, with proxy education level being a significant determinant of agreement.
Derive Danish preference-based weights for the EQ-5D-5L using standardised EQ-VT protocol and explore discrete choice methodology with novel task formats.

age_group: general public respondents valuing health states from perspectives of 8-year-old children and 40-year-old adults
key_finding: Adult respondents assign significantly higher utility values to child health states compared to adult health states across multiple valuation methods, driven by principles of intergenerational responsibility and differences in perceived capacity for decision-making and coping.

This study aims to understand why adults value health states differently for themselves compared to children and adolescents, and how age and duration influence these valuations using qualitative methods alongside valuation tasks.
This project will simultaneously elicit value sets and develop population norms for both EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L in Romania using cTTO and DCE methods in a nationally representative sample.

This study evaluates the psychometric performance and responsiveness of the EQ-5D-5L with cognition and fatigue bolt-on items in sarcoma and colorectal cancer patients to determine if bolt-ons improve measurement of cancer-specific HRQoL.
Exploration of public perspectives on differences between hypothetical and experienced health state valuations and acceptable solutions to reconcile such differences.
Assessment of test-retest reliability of EQ-5D-5L administered via web-based survey compared to in-person interview in general populations across three countries.

age_group: children and young adults aged 12-25 years
key_finding: Differences in index values between EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-5L vary by country, with Asian countries showing higher values on EQ-5D-Y-3L while European countries and Australia show lower values, potentially affecting QALY calculations in longitudinal assessments and health technology appraisals.

This study aims to evaluate methods for presenting EQ-5D data in U.S. rheumatology clinical practice and assess stakeholder preferences for visualization formats to enhance patient-centered care and clinical decision-making.

Psychological distance between adult valuers and the child being valued significantly influences cTTO utilities for EQ-5D-Y-3L health states, with effects moderated by parental status and adult sociocultural characteristics such as conservatism and collectivism.

This qualitative study explores the content validity, relevance, and cognitive interpretation of the EQ-5D questionnaire and EQ-VAS among Asian populations to assess the appropriateness of the instrument for use in China, Japan, South Korea, and Singapore.

Incorporating power functions into cTTO-based weight estimation requires protocol modifications and integration of DCE data to address limitations in interval estimation and proportionality assumptions.

This exploratory study investigates whether pictorial enhancements can support younger children's understanding and self-completion of the EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L, potentially extending the self-reported age range below eight years.

This systematic review will identify and synthesize methodologies used to value child and adolescent health states across generic and condition-specific preference-based measures to inform future EQ-5D-Y valuation protocols.

EQ-5D instruments have substantially greater value set availability and geographic coverage compared to other multi-attribute utility instruments, with EQ-5D-5L showing higher methodological standardisation than EQ-5D-3L.

This project aims to conduct a systematic Dutch translation of four EQ-5D-5L bolt-ons (breathing, fatigue, sleep, cognition) and 18 exploratory items following EuroQol's Version Management Control guidelines, including forward/backward translations and cognitive debriefing interviews.

This systematic review will provide a comprehensive overview of published studies on the psychometric performance of EQ-5D bolt-on dimensions, including their formats, origins, study settings, and performance metrics.
A training workshop was conducted to educate participants on EQ-5D methodology and application in the Chinese context.
Development of a value set for the EQ-5D-5L in Italy using composite time trade-off and discrete choice experiment methods.

This project develops a conceptual framework to address challenges in using EQ-5D-Y for economic evaluation in children, including issues with score ranges, QALY equivalence, and discontinuities in cost-effectiveness models spanning childhood to adulthood.

A value set for the EQ-5D-5L was derived from the Greek general population using a hybrid heteroskedastic model combining cTTO and DCE data, representing the first implementation of EQ-VT version 2.1 in Greece.
Testing the ranking exercise for EQ-5D-Y-5L severity levels to inform instrument validation and potential promotion from beta to improved version status.
Dynamic prediction models using longitudinal EQ-5D measurements can predict injury recovery prognosis and identify patients with poor outcomes.
This study examines the consistency between discrete choice experiment and composite time trade-off valuation methods for EQ-5D-5L in Japan to assess cross-cultural validity in Asian populations.

Preference heterogeneity in discrete choice experiments can lead to biased conditional logit estimates of EQ-5D-5L values, with willingness-to-pay differences up to 20%, highlighting the importance of accounting for heterogeneity in health preference valuation studies.
To compare the psychometric properties of EQ-5D-5L versus EQ-5D-3L in self- and proxy-reported assessments of health-related quality of life in cognitively impaired patients with dementia.

A new conceptual framework of health developed among children and adolescents in Malawi contains seven concepts, four of which align with EQ-5D-Y dimensions but five concepts are not captured by the EQ-5D-Y, suggesting the instrument may not fully represent health concepts in low-income country populations.
This study examines the comparability of scoring functions and value sets between EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L in the US to inform the transition between instruments.
To determine the validity, reliability and feasibility of the EQ-5D-Y-3L interviewer administered version in children aged 5-8 years compared to older children and the self-complete version.
