A new Polish EQ-5D-5L value set was developed using hybrid cTTO and DCE data with improved sensitivity to mild health worsening while maintaining consistency with existing value sets.
A team of EuroQol researchers from Singapore visited Canada to attend conferences, present EQ-5D studies, and explore research collaborations to establish an EQ-5D support unit in Singapore.

EQ-5D health state utilities require rescaling before interpersonal comparison and aggregation into social value sets, particularly when individuals differ in whether they consider health states worse than dead.

The EQ VAS primarily measures health-related quality of life through proximal health concepts (EQ-5D items, functional limitations, and presence of illness) rather than serving as a general self-rated health measure, with design elements reflecting its original valuation purpose rather than health measurement.
statistical_methods: partial least squares structural equation modelling

age_group: representative sample stratified by age and gender
key_finding: Generate a value set for Belgium using composite time trade-off and discrete choice experiment tasks with hybrid modeling approaches to assess health state preferences.
Gain/loss framing had limited influence on EQ-5D-5L valuations in both DCE and TTO methods, with implications for cross-method comparability in value set derivation.
This study will validate and compare the psychometric properties of the EQ-5D-3L-Y and EQ-5D-5L-Y in US children and adolescents with arthritis, leukemia, and healthy controls.
A value set for the EQ-5D-5L was developed for the Vietnam population using time trade-off methodology.
EQ-5D-5L value set for Singapore was estimated using composite TTO data and compared with previous EQ-VT results to investigate socio-demographic factors affecting health state valuations.

The Better than Dead method is feasible and reliable for valuing EQ-5D health states, with religious life stance and educational level as important determinants of preferences for states worse than dead.
Translation of EQ-5D analytical methods guidance into Chinese to support proper data analysis and reporting practices among Chinese-speaking researchers.

The optimized bifactor model confirms that the UK EQ-HWB structure fits the Chinese population, with the instrument demonstrating sensitivity to disease burden in physical and mental health conditions.
A preference-weighted model for EQ-5D-5L health states was successfully developed for the Korean population using composite time trade-off and discrete choice experiment data.

This mixed-methods study evaluates five possible VAS anchors for the EQ-HWB-9 to determine the most appropriate anchor for inclusion, using both manual content analysis and AI-assisted analytical approaches.

age_group: stratified by age and sex across representative sample
key_finding: Thai population-based preference scores for EQ-5D-5L were successfully developed using lead-time TTO and DCE methods, with mobility identified as the dimension with greatest impact on preference scores.
Describe health-related quality of life during pregnancy and postpartum using EQ-5D-5L in a large nationwide cohort and examine health inequities and predictors of postnatal health outcomes.

Happiness is only a segment of subjective well-being measures, which are themselves only a segment of broader well-being measures, suggesting that health status measurement requires more sophisticated approaches beyond happiness metrics.
Examine the validity and responsiveness of the EQ-5D-Y-5L self-report version in children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis and compare results to parent-proxy versions.

The EQ-5D-3L demonstrates acceptable psychometric properties including validity, reliability, and responsiveness in patients with rare ataxia diseases, with disease progression, mental health, and obesity identified as key factors influencing health-related quality of life decline.
EuroQol Asian Academy Meeting promotes EQ-5D research collaboration and knowledge sharing among Asian researchers in health-related quality of life and health technology assessment studies.

Health valuations vary by country and cultural context, and Latin American decision makers should prioritize collecting direct local valuation data for EQ-5D rather than relying on indirect derivation methods.
A workshop on preference-based health measures and EQ valuation methods was well-received by 12 attendees with varying levels of experience, demonstrating strong interest in valuation research.
Regional workshop to engage EQ-5D users and HTA policy makers in Asia-Pacific region.
Crosswalk and EQ-VT derived EQ-5D-5L value sets show poor agreement and should not be used interchangeably except in countries with populations under 250,000.

To establish a theoretical foundation for introducing gender-neutral language in EuroQol instruments by conducting a scoping review of strategies used in questionnaire design and engaging specialist advisors from LGBTQIA+ and culturally diverse communities.

To assess health inequalities measured through EQ-5D in Dutch patients undergoing hip and knee arthroplasty for osteoarthritis, with hypotheses that better outcomes and higher surgical gain occur with higher socioeconomic status and that larger inequalities are observed with EQ-5D index compared to VAS.

A framework identifying sources of variability in EQ-5D values and a novel method for calculating standard errors around health state profile values to strengthen uncertainty handling in cost-effectiveness analysis.

Establish EQ-5D population norms and health trajectories from the Stockholm Public Health Cohort to enable comparison of patient populations in Swedish national quality registries and assess health inequalities across sociodemographic groups.

Case 2 BWS scores are related to DCE-derived values but respondents apply different weights to attributes, particularly when experiencing impairment, suggesting BWS may capture experienced utility effects.

age_group: mixed ages including younger and older respondents
key_finding: EQ-5D-5L demonstrated improved discriminative performance with reduced ceiling effects (34.9% vs 44.4%) compared to EQ-5D-3L, though both versions showed comparable standardized effect sizes across groups with known health differences.

age_group: general adult population, with subsample aged ≥65 years (n=453)
key_finding: The EQ-HWB demonstrated robust psychometric performance in an Australian population with moderate reliability, strong convergent validity with EQ-5D-5L, and the 25-item version explained more variance in external quality of life measures than the 9-item version.
Development of EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L value sets for the adult population in Bangladesh using the standard EuroQol valuation protocol.

Mode of administration significantly impacts measurement properties of pediatric HRQoL scales, with greater discrepancies between self-administered and interviewer-administered modes than between digital and paper-based modes.

To assess the construct validity of the EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S as measures of spillover among carers and wider family members through discriminant and convergent validity testing against the EQ-5D-5L and CarerQol.
Population health status was measured using EQ-5D instruments during the early weeks of the coronavirus pandemic and compared with pre-pandemic baseline data from the Health Survey for England.

age_group: 65 years and over (primary analysis); general population (secondary analysis)
key_finding: EQ-5D dimensions capturing physical and mental health, particularly self-care and pain/discomfort, are significantly associated with social care needs in older adults, suggesting potential for EQ-5D to measure social care outcomes.

age_group: mean age 33.8 years, predominantly single mothers
key_finding: EQ-HWB demonstrated moderate test-retest reliability and strong convergent validity with EQ-5D-5L and SWEMWBS, but showed inconsistent responses in 33% of participants when transitioning between negative and positive items.

age_group: caregivers of children and adolescents aged 8 to 17
key_finding: This study examines the content validity of the EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S in caregivers of pediatric individuals with autism spectrum disorder to identify whether these instruments adequately capture health-related quality of life and wellbeing in this population.

This systematic review evaluates the methodological quality and appropriateness of validity, reliability, and responsiveness studies of EQ-5D-5L to inform future psychometric validation guidelines for EuroQol instruments.
To identify what aspects of health are important to people and generate candidate domains for a new generic health classification system beyond the existing EQ-5D descriptive system.

EQ-5D-5L demonstrated construct validity in the Lebanese general population during severe socio-economic crisis, with pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression being highly prevalent, and HRQoL significantly associated with food insecurity and psychological distress.
Introduction of the Indonesian EQ-5D-5L value set and population norm scores to facilitate implementation and cost-effectiveness analysis in Indonesia's health insurance system.
A representative EQ-5D-5L value set for Taiwan was derived using hybrid modeling with utility values ranging from -1.0259 to 1.

The novel pTTO method demonstrated superior performance compared to cTTO for valuing EQ-5D-5L health states, particularly for severe states, with less value clustering, higher logical consistency, and better discriminatory ability.
Workshop on new measurement and analytic approaches for determining utility of multi-attribute health states, focusing on DCE modeling, quality control, and heteroscedastic regression methods.
This project aims to examine the feasibility and psychometric properties of the EQ-HWB-S and multiple potential cognition bolt-on items for the EQ-5D-5L in dementia patients.
Feasibility and operational value of routine EQ-5D measurement in NHS community mental health services for real-time clinical decision-making.

age_group: mean age 14 years, children and youths
key_finding: The internet-administered EQ-5D-Y shows good sensitivity and specificity for detecting changes in health-related quality of life in children and youths with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus in clinical practice, with high capacity for detecting improvement.
EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S demonstrated good psychometric properties with lower ceiling effects than EQ-5D-5L, capturing both health-related quality of life and broader wellbeing aspects.

age_group: adults valuing health states for themselves and for a 10-year-old child
key_finding: Four anchoring methods (VAS, DCE with duration, lead-time TTO, and location-of-dead PUF) showed broad agreement in valuing EQ-5D-Y health states, with consistently lower values from an adult perspective compared to a child perspective.

age_group: adults valuing health states for themselves and for a 10-year-old child
key_finding: Four anchoring methods (VAS, DCE with duration, lead-time TTO, and location-of-dead PUF) showed broad agreement in valuing EQ-5D-Y health states, with consistently lower values under adult perspective compared to child perspective.

Present personal health experience at the point of valuation led to higher EQ-5D valuations, but no statistically significant causal effects of past personal or vicarious experience with severe illness on health state valuations were detected.

A head-to-head comparison of EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L value sets across eight countries and patient groups identified four factors (descriptive performance, distributional effects, valuation effects, and country-specific effects) underlying differences in discriminatory power between versions.
SEVQoL investigates whether people show preference for prioritising the worse off in hypothetical healthcare allocation scenarios using individually calibrated EQ-5D-5L health state values.

EQ-5D versions were most frequently evaluated and generally performed well in older adults, though ceiling effects and responsiveness issues were reported, while ICECAP-O and ASCOT showed strong evidence but need further testing on responsiveness.
Allocation efficiency in DCE studies for EQ-5D-5L valuation is optimized with >50 responses per pair and approximately 150 pairs, with attention to scale and level balance in design.

age_group: adolescents 11-17 years and adults; adolescents rating own health, adults rating health of 10-year-old child
key_finding: Adolescents' preferences for EQ-5D-Y health states differ significantly from adults' preferences when considering a child's health, with differences not explained by scale alone, suggesting adolescents are capable of completing DCE valuation tasks.
statistical_methods: mixed logit models with correlated parameters

key_finding: Establish infrastructure for the EQ Group to assess population health using EQ instruments across multiple countries.

age_group: mean age 40±18.1 years, range appears to span adults
key_finding: Participants experienced confusion about the distinction between same-as-dead and worse-than-dead valuations and the transition from tTTO to LT-TTO in the EQVT platform, resulting in apparently arbitrary health state valuations around this transition.

EQ-5D-5L utility values derived using composite TTO are not significantly affected by whether full health or 11111 is used as the comparator health state, though vision and energy were identified as potentially important health dimensions not currently captured.

This study investigates barriers and facilitators to integrating patient-reported outcomes into routine clinical care for head and neck cancer services, focusing on healthcare professionals' perspectives.
A visit to establish stakeholder engagement and develop EuroQol projects using EQ-5D and PROMs in the Singapore health system to inform clinical decision-making.
DCEtto successfully generated EQ-5D-5L values with better distribution for severe health states than TTO, but with lower cardinal values and limited consistency between the two protocols.

Girls reported significantly higher rates of problems across anxiety/sadness dimensions compared to boys, with rates doubling in older girls, and overall deterioration in self-reported health status compared to surveys from 10 years prior.

The Lay Concepts Study elicited how ordinary people conceptualize health through face-to-face interviews with disabled and able-bodied young adults, carers, and general population members to inform the development of the EQ-5D descriptive system.
An 8-parameter multiplicative regression model performed best for generating an EQ-5D-5L value set for China based on time trade-off preferences from urban residents.

This study compares the impact of different mental health descriptors ('Feeling worried, sad or unhappy' vs 'Anxiety/Depression') on EQ-5D valuation using DCE methods to support transitions between age-specific EQ-5D instruments.
Testing the feasibility and validity of intensive longitudinal assessment using EQ-5D-5L to capture fluctuating health impairments in multiple sclerosis patients.
Development of a structured e-learning program to educate end-users and researchers on EuroQol instruments and methods for measuring and valuing health-related quality of life.

age_group: across lifespan, with gaps in youth and elderly representation
key_finding: Existing generic preference-based instruments like EQ-5D may have inadequate content coverage from the patient perspective, particularly lacking representation of youth and elderly populations and not fully capturing patient-centered health attributes.
EQ-5D data can serve as a linking mechanism between datasets across multiple public sectors (health, local authorities, criminal justice) beyond traditional health applications.
REDCap platform evaluation for constructing EQ-5D-5L valuation survey instruments using discrete choice experiments in the United States and Germany.

age_group: 10, 15, and 40 years (hypothetical persons rated by general population)
key_finding: Health state values derived from DCE show strong agreement across age groups when controlling for time preferences, except for pain which is valued lower for children.
This study evaluates the psychometric properties of EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S in Chinese patients with anxiety or depression, comparing original and modified versions.

Examination of the internal structure of the EQ-HWB across three general population datasets to confirm structural validity and assess measurement effects of positively and negatively framed items across languages and countries.

The EQ-5D-5L demonstrated sufficient responsiveness in detecting health changes in people living with dementia, particularly in those receiving collaborative care intervention and experiencing cognitive or emotional improvement, outperforming the disease-specific QoL-AD scale in several subgroups.

The EQ-5D-5L exhibited meaningful age-related differential item functioning for anxiety/depression but not for gender or education, suggesting response behavior is generally stable across gender and education groups but varies by age.
Workshop demonstrating how to measure and value patient preferences using EQ-5D-5L in randomized clinical trials for cost-effectiveness analysis.
A feasibility study comparing web-based and paper-and-pencil EQ-5D administration methods across demographic characteristics, recruitment efficiency, and data robustness.

Systematic review to evaluate how EuroQol instruments have been applied to assess health inequalities and synthesize evidence on their sensitivity to capture inequalities across sociodemographic and socioeconomic subgroups.
This qualitative study explores stakeholder perspectives on the feasibility and expectations of a proposed multi-level hierarchical EQ-5D with dimension-specific modules nested below core dimensions.
Testing face and content validity of the QALY framework with patients, social-care users and carers in Germany using qualitative interviews in China.
EQ-HWB items outperformed existing EQ-5D-5L-format bolt-ons in overall psychometric performance, with sleep and exhaustion emerging as the most promising bolt-on candidates in breast cancer patients.

Regret minimization (RRM) better describes choice behavior than utility maximization (RUM) when respondents face different survival scenarios, with semi-compensatory decision-making patterns observed.
Anchoring health state values at 'dead = 0' is not a theoretical requirement for QALY estimation and should be reconsidered due to methodological and conceptual problems it creates.

This study compares the construct validity and responsiveness of EQ-HWB-S and EQ-5D-5L in Chinese gastrointestinal cancer patients undergoing anticancer treatment to evaluate whether the broader EQ-HWB-S better captures health and well-being outcomes compared to the EQ-5D-5L.
A Norwegian EQ-5D-5L value set was developed using a hybrid model combining cTTO and DCE data, with anxiety/depression identified as the most highly valued dimension.

The EQ-HWB showed general answerability among informal dementia carers but revealed perspective ambiguity, caregiving phase effects, and missing constructs including identity loss and anticipatory worry.

age_group: general population representative of sex, age and education
key_finding: DCE is feasible for valuing EQ-HWB with 13 attributes, with both DCETTO and DCE-Death tasks producing valid preference data, though results vary by task design and country.
This study evaluated the psychometric properties of composite items in the EQ-HWB/EQ-HWB-S using modern test theory to compare merged double-barreled items against their single-domain counterparts.

The EQ-HWB-S will be tested for validity and suitability in patients with rare neuromuscular conditions and their carers through cognitive debriefing interviews and psychometric analysis against condition-specific measures and clinical outcomes.
Comparison of DCE with duration attribute and cTTO methods for valuing EQ-5D-Y-5L to develop a pediatric value set.
A research visit to four universities to facilitate collaborative working on EQ-related research projects and build networks in long-term care and Asia.

age_group: mean age 41 years, aged 18 years and older
key_finding: Follow-up of neurosurgery patients by telephone one month after discharge is feasible, with high proportions reporting difficulties in mobility, self-care, and usual activities despite improvement from pre-discharge.

Testing psychometric properties of EQ-TIPS-3L and EQ-TIPS-5L versions to refine the descriptive system and ensure international validity for measuring health-related quality of life in toddlers and infants.

age_group: mean age 46.6-48.6 years, range includes 30 to 74 years
key_finding: Online cognitive debriefing interviews are feasible for general populations with adequate digital skills and internet access, but face-to-face approaches remain more suitable for older and less technically proficient populations.

age_group: general public respondents valuing health states for 8-year-old children and 40-year-old adults
key_finding: Adult respondents assign significantly higher utility values to child health states compared to adult health states across multiple valuation methods, driven by beliefs about childhood as a foundation period and parental responsibility.

Time trade-off and discrete choice experiment preference elicitation methods are feasible, practical, and acceptable for use with the Pakistani population, including illiterate respondents when supported by graphical illustrations.

A new conceptual framework of child health in Malawi with seven domains shows partial overlap with EQ-5D-Y domains but includes three culturally unique domains (God-given, strength/energy, acceptance of illness) and lacks representation of pain, suggesting potential content validity limitations of EQ-5D-Y in low-income country contexts.

The OPUF approach has potential to generate personal EQ-5D-5L value sets for individual patients to support clinical decision-making by identifying which health problems are most important from the patient's perspective.

The project aims to analyze sociodemographic inequalities and temporal trends in EQ-5D disability patterns to develop population norms for Estonia and inform health policy on addressing health inequalities.
An exploratory methodology study using online PUF approach to value EQ-5D-5L bolt-on dimensions in the general population.

Differences between Classic and Chained TTO utilities are primarily explained by different evaluation modes (separate vs. joint) rather than anchoring effects, with preference reversals being a key driver of the disparity.

A hybrid cTTO-DCE model successfully estimated an EQ-5D-5L value set for cancer patients, revealing that cancer patients weight pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression more heavily than the general population.
Research visit to facilitate collaborative work on EQ-based projects and develop bolt-on dimensions relevant to older adults.
The EQ-5D-5L only partially captures fatigue and cognition problems in Q-fever patients, with addition of fatigue dimension slightly improving explained variance for EQ VAS.

age_group: adult patients and parents of children
key_finding: Assessment of psychometric properties of EQ-5D-5L, EQ-HWB, and EQ-5D-Y-5L in rare genetic disease populations to inform health technology assessment decisions in genomic medicine.

Each of the five bolt-ons (hearing, sleep, cognition, energy, relationships) significantly impacts public preferences for EQ-5D-5L health states, with the magnitude of impact varying by bolt-on severity level and the health state to which they are added.
statistical_methods: statistical testing of differences in proportions

key_finding: International research collaboration meeting to develop a protocol for EQ-5D valuation research in China.

Chronic disease patients (heart disease and cancer) show different utility value patterns compared to the general population, with implications for cost-effectiveness analyses using disease-specific versus general population value sets.
QALY-balanced DCE designs reduce bias in health state valuation by ensuring adequate coverage of the severity range, particularly for DCE-duration approaches.
This study will develop a Qatar-specific EQ-5D-5L value set and compare the consistency of value sets derived from TTO-based, hybrid, and DCE with duration methodologies.

A large number of EQ-5D-derived health state utilities for hematologic malignant neoplasms was identified from 54 papers, with substantial variation in utility values across disease types and notable gaps in availability between different hematologic malignancies.
Study visit to develop collaborative research proposals on EQ instrument recall periods, data quality in preference elicitation, and routine outcome assessment applications.

Respondents can assess their own imprecision in health state preferences using extended TTO methodology, with imprecision larger than standard TTO estimation error and driven primarily by uncertainty about usual activities dimension.

Ukrainian refugees in Estonia demonstrated significantly lower health-related quality of life compared to age and sex-matched general population peers, with behavioral risk factors each decreasing EQ-5D index values by 0.04.

Government response stringency had small positive effects on HRQL but strong negative effects on mental well-being during the first phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, with differential impacts across health status groups.

age_group: adults valuing health states for hypothetical 10-year-old children
key_finding: Composite time trade-off values differ between adult and child perspectives, particularly for severe health states, with differences partially explained by respondent characteristics including education, region, parental status, and beliefs about child versus adult life value.
Comparison of psychometric properties, feasibility, informativity and redistribution characteristics of EQ-5D-5L-Y versus EQ-5D-3L-Y in pediatric scoliosis patients in Hong Kong.

age_group: older adults aged ≥60 years (with caregivers aged ≥18 years)
key_finding: This study will evaluate the psychometric properties, reliability, measurement error, construct validity, and responsiveness of the EQ-HWB-9 proxy interviewer-administered version in Brazilian frail and non-frail older adults.

FEDEV aims to improve discrete choice experiment with duration (DCETTO) methodology for EQ-5D-5L valuation by optimizing duration attributes, exploring alternative design and modelling approaches, and examining effects of dimension presentation and severity trade-offs.
Consistency between EQ-5D-5L and bolt-on value sets can be achieved through modest disutility reductions of 2-17% to eliminate double-counting while preserving measurement sensitivity.
A level sum score and two subscales for EQ-HWB-S were validated, with 3- and 6-factor models recommended for EQ-HWB scoring pending confirmation with current instrument version data.

Qualitative exploration of whether strengths-based adaptations to the EQ-5D-Y-5L are needed from consumer and expert perspectives to improve inclusivity for children with life-limiting conditions or complex disabilities.

Bayesian models with spatial correlation improve the predictive precision of EQ-5D-5L value sets compared to published linear models, reducing root mean squared errors across all seven countries studied.

This systematic review will assess the extent to which EQ-5D and other generic HRQoL measures have been used to evaluate health outcomes associated with extreme weather events and climate change impacts, and examine their measurement properties across different populations and settings.

Individual-level concerns about SARS-CoV-2 variants are associated with lower health-related quality of life, predominantly through increased anxiety and depression, while aggregate-level HRQoL was lowest for individuals birthing early in the pandemic.
Development of a Tunisian value set for the EQ-5D-3L using a hybrid valuation approach combining TTO and VAS methods.
Assessment of construct validity and psychometric comparability of EQ-HWB-S and cognition bolt-ons alongside EQ-5D-5L in an Argentine elderly nursing home population.
Assessment of the feasibility and content validity of the EQ-VT TTO protocol for valuing child health states in older adolescents aged 16-17 years.

Development of Brazilian guidelines for utility measurement selection and hierarchy in health technology assessment and cost-utility analysis to improve transparency and prevent flawed modeling practices.

Personal present experience with health states is associated with higher TTO valuations compared to non-experienced-based values, while vicarious experience of serious illness in others is associated with lower valuations.

age_group: adults with spread of age groups
key_finding: To psychometrically evaluate the measurement properties of the EQ-5D-5L and four bolt-ons (skin irritation, self-confidence, sleep, and social relationships) in patients with chronic urticaria.

This study will explore the content validity of the EQ-5D-5L with skin irritation and self-confidence bolt-ons in alopecia areata and vitiligo to determine their comprehensiveness, comprehensibility, and relevance in these dermatological conditions.

The choice of EQ-5D utility scoring method (value sets versus crosswalks) can significantly impact cost-utility outcomes and reimbursement decisions, particularly when treatment effect sizes are small.

Cross-cultural adaptation of EQ-TIPS into Chichewa identified significant challenges in translating emotional and abstract concepts, particularly managing emotions, pain, sleep, and social interaction, requiring expansion of examples and age-appropriate terminology for accurate measurement in African language settings.
Family members are the most feasible and accurate proxies for estimating pre-admission quality of life in incapacitated ICU patients compared to physicians and general practitioners.

This study aims to translate, culturally adapt, and psychometrically validate EQ-TIPS-5L and EQ-HWB-9 in Egyptian caregivers of young children with and without malignancies to support wider application in Egypt and the MENA region.
Evaluation of psychometric properties of the EQ-5D-5L skin bolt-on dimension in patients with mild-to-moderate psoriasis using longitudinal clinical trial data.
Development of guidance on design and analysis considerations for using EQ-5D in randomized controlled trials and observational studies to inform cost-effectiveness models.

Workshop disseminated state-of-the-art EuroQol research on TTO valuation techniques and EQ-5D-5L value set development, identifying future research needs for improving TTO validity and exploring interval regression for modeling TTO data.

age_group: adults aged 18 years and above for cTTO and DCE; adolescents aged 10-17 years for DCE tasks
key_finding: cTTO and DCE methods show high agreement with consistent pain/discomfort dominance across dimensions, and no statistically significant differences between adult and adolescent preferences, supporting a combined cTTO and latent-scale DCE design for the Indian EQ-5D-Y-5L value set development.
statistical_methods: mixed logit model with exponential discounting

key_finding: The study aims to validate the EQ-HWB-S and determine its responsiveness to change in people living with dementia with mild cognitive decline participating in a residential aged care reablement intervention.

This project explores heterogeneity in stakeholder views on involving children in EQ-5D-Y-3L valuation studies, examining how experience with valuation methods, parental status, and child age affect support for children's participation.

This study compares DCE with duration attribute and cTTO methods for valuing the EQ-5D-Y-5L to develop a Polish value set and test whether these methods produce similar results for paediatric utility instruments.

EQ-5D demonstrates good to fair psychometric properties across most conditions studied, but has particular limitations in capturing the impact of dementia, schizophrenia, visual impairment, and hearing disorders.
EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrates superior test-retest reliability and sensitivity to health changes compared to EQ-5D-Y-3L, with both versions showing comparable convergent validity.

This study investigates cross-cultural interpretation of response options in EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S instruments across four countries to assess validity and consistency in scoring across diverse populations.
EQ-5D-Y-5L is feasible with lower ceiling effects and higher discriminative power than EQ-5D-Y-3L in children with cancer.

A systematic review identified 21 publications on vision bolt-ons and 8 on hearing bolt-ons for EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L, summarizing development methods, wording variations, populations tested, and psychometric evidence.

This secondary data analysis evaluates whether internet panel quota sampling can achieve representativeness comparable to random sampling for EQ-5D-5L population norms by comparing health and sociodemographic distributions across four UK surveys using different sampling approaches.

This study assesses the validity of proposed modifications to EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S items and response options in a mixed patient and social care user population using cognitive interviewing and framework analysis.

EQ-5D-3L rank-based data is best represented unidimensionally, supporting the assumption that quality-adjusted life-years are unidimensional despite some statistical evidence for two-dimensional improvement.
This study develops a Japanese value set for EQ-5D-Y-5L and compares the consistency between composite time trade-off and discrete choice experiment valuation methods.

EQ-5D-5L demonstrates superior descriptive responsiveness compared to EQ-5D-3L in both rehabilitation and stroke patients, with better value responsiveness in rehabilitation but not in stroke, primarily driven by descriptive system differences and 3L overestimation bias.

The 2nd EuroQol Asia Academy Meeting aims to continue fostering collaboration and knowledge sharing among Asian researchers on EQ-5D applications, with focus on culturally-specific dimensions, valuation studies, and methods for difficult-to-reach populations.

The EQ-5D-5L/3L demonstrates generally good psychometric performance in people with haemophilia, with evidence of known-group validity, convergent validity, and responsiveness, though reliability evidence is limited.

The EQ-5D-5L demonstrates mixed evidence of psychometric properties in conditions where itch is a key symptom, with evidence for known-groups validity and convergent validity but insufficient evidence for responsiveness, suggesting potential value of a skin irritation (itch) bolt-on.

The modified EQ-HWB-S performed better or similarly to the original version across most psychometric domains, with stronger convergent validity at instrument level, but showed limited effectiveness in differentiating between carers and non-carers.

It is feasible to generate meaningful EQ-5D-5L health-state values in the UAE using standardized valuation protocols, though some methodological adaptations may be needed for Arab and Muslim populations.
EuroQol sponsorship of the IAHPR 2025 meeting increased visibility and engagement within the health preference research community, with at least 8-9 EuroQol members attending.

This study investigates whether preference-weighted versus sum-scored EQ-HWB-S affect psychometric properties including known-group validity and change over time across multiple international datasets.

This project will assess country-related differential item functioning across EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB-9 using the EQ-DAPHNIE dataset to determine which instrument demonstrates greater cross-country measurement invariance.

Changing the order of EQ-5D questions produces small but measurable order effects, particularly for pain/discomfort and anxiety/depression questions when asked first, with effects most pronounced among healthy respondents.

This study evaluates the feasibility, reliability, validity, and inter-mode comparability of self-complete, interviewer-administered, and proxy versions of EQ-HWB-9 among hospitalized older adults in China.
Translation of 31 items from the EQ-5D Bolt-on Toolbox into Polish with cognitive debriefing validation to ensure cultural appropriateness and clarity for use in the EQ-DAPHNIE population survey.

To explore how the COVID-19 pandemic and its legacy as well as current economic circumstances differentially impact health-related quality of life across diverse populations in different socioeconomic settings and countries.
This project will develop user-friendly visualisation formats for EQ-5D-5L data to improve understanding and facilitate implementation in routine clinical care for patients with sciatica.

The EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S demonstrated good psychometric performance in caregivers of persons living with dementia, with acceptable distribution, strong known groups validity, and convergent validity, though four items showed poor factor loading.
EQ-HWB-9 shows a positive relationship with age unlike EQ-5D-5L, with physical problems increasing but psychosocial problems decreasing across the life course.
EQ-5D-5L is a feasible and valid metric in critically ill patients with moderate-to-strong correlation to EQ-VAS, though it tends to underestimate health utility compared to SF-6D conversions.

Adults are reluctant to assign worse-than-dead values to child health states due to viewing childhood life as inherently valuable, perceiving dependency as manageable with support, and only considering death acceptable when children lack meaningful daily activity.

This study compares three strategies for linking bolt-on dimensions to existing EQ-5D value sets and two types of discrete choice experiments to develop cost-effective and reliable valuation approaches for extended EQ-5D instruments.
EQ-5D-Y-5L questionnaire is valuable for remote monitoring of patients with juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

Interaction terms significantly improve EQ-5D valuation models, with broader health state coverage yielding better predictive accuracy than increasing observations per state, and optimal model specifications differing between EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L versions.
95% of people living with dementia rated their health differently than their caregivers, with caregivers tending to rate health more conservatively, particularly in observable domains.

A researcher-led meeting was held to discuss recent developments in EuroQol instruments and their applications, primarily engaging UK and Ireland-based researchers including early career researchers and students.

Incorporating supplemental pairwise choice tasks and Maximum Endurable Time into DCE improved statistical identification and anchoring of value sets to cTTO benchmarks, though formal MET modeling could not be reliably fitted.

Spanish translation of EQ-TIPS version 3.0 for Argentina in both 3L and 5L versions was completed following cognitive debriefing results that informed modifications to the descriptive system, item wording, and response scale labels.
Development and application of an open-source Julia package (MIOP.jl) to detect and quantify response heterogeneity and mis-reporting bias in EQ-5D self-reports across heterogeneous populations.
A Saudi-specific value set for the EQ-5D-5L was successfully developed, with pain and discomfort having the largest impact on health-state preferences.

To empirically test whether appending a bolt-on dimension at level 1 to core EQ-5D-5L health states increases utility, decreases utility, or leaves utility unchanged, and whether this effect generalizes across bolt-ons with different causal linkages to core dimensions.
This study evaluates respondent burden of the EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S in men with prostate cancer to guide instrument selection in clinical practice.

This project evaluates how multidimensional socioeconomic disadvantage is associated with COVID-19 and long-COVID symptoms and their impact on health-related quality of life in India across diverse states.
EQ-5D health dimensions are cross-culturally considered the most important aspects for describing poor health across seven geographically and culturally diverse countries.

This is the first comprehensive assessment of EQ-HWB psychometric properties in frail elderly across multiple care settings in China, evaluating feasibility, acceptability, validity, and responsiveness for routine geriatric rehabilitation quality-of-life assessment.

This study examines associations between health literacy and health-related quality of life and well-being outcomes measured by EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB-9 in a general population sample to inform interpretation and support measurement validity.
statistical_methods: partial proportional odds ordinal logistic regression

key_finding: Seven-day recall periods tend to produce higher symptom severity and lower quality of life scores compared to one-day recall periods across generic health domains, with patient preferences varying by condition characteristics and concept type.
Testing whether preferences for bolt-on dimensions can be inferred from core EQ-5D value sets to reduce sample sizes and facilitate preference transfer across countries.
EQ-DAPHNIE is establishing a multi-country primary data collection infrastructure to generate population norms and compare EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB instruments across diverse populations.

age_group: children aged 0-48 months and their caregivers
key_finding: This study will comprehensively validate EQ-TIPS and evaluate caregiver spillover effects using EQ-5D-5L bolt-ons and EQ-HWB-S in early childhood populations across acute, chronic, and healthy conditions.

This project aims to develop best practice guidelines (CREATE-CI) for conducting and reporting collaborative involvement of patients, public, caregivers, and decision-makers in health state valuation studies.
EQ-5D-3L self-care dimension can replace clinician-assessed performance status in predicting survival in advanced incurable cancer, with prognostic value varying by time to death.
Evaluate and compare the psychometric properties of EQ-5D-5L, five bolt-ons and EQ-HWB-S in injury patients to determine their reliability and validity for clinical practice and research adoption.

EQ-5D-Y instruments demonstrated acceptable reliability and validity in children with osteogenesis imperfecta, with EQ-5D-Y-3L showing slightly better convergent validity and discriminative ability than EQ-5D-Y-5L.

age_group: adult respondents valuing health states for 10-year-old children
key_finding: Parent TTO and lag-time TTO methods produce lower values more similar to EQ-5D-5L but do not improve acceptability or feasibility compared to cTTO for EQ-5D-Y valuation.

An international protocol for valuing the EQ-5D-Y combines time trade-off and discrete-choice experiments to elicit adult preferences for child health states, raising methodological questions about whose preferences should count and consistency between child and adult valuation approaches.

The EQ-HWB-S performs comparably to EQ-5D-5L in discriminating between known groups with strong convergence between conceptually overlapping dimensions, though a potentially problematic skewed distribution was identified in the EQ-HWB-S mobility domain.

This project aims to co-design an improved, child-friendly EQ-5D-Y valuation and interview protocol by engaging children, adolescents, parents, paediatric experts, and valuation experts in collaborative design.
To validate the psychometric properties of the EQ-5D-Y-5L and EQ-HWB-9 among patients and caregivers with inherited bleeding disorders in Canada.

This study explores response shift in EQ-5D data among knee arthroplasty patients using item response theory methods to improve the validity of healthcare decisions based on patient-reported outcomes.
statistical_methods: ROSALI (response shift algorithm in item response theory)

key_finding: This study will compare the psychometric performance of five energy- and sleep-related EQ-5D-5L bolt-ons (tiredness, energy, fatigue, exhaustion, and sleep) across six countries to identify which best captures fatigue/energy and sleep in the general population.

An entry-level workshop on EQ-5D technologies can serve as a catalyst to encourage adoption of standardized health status measurement systems in Russia and neighboring countries with limited prior experience in health economics and HTA methods.

This research program will develop and refine the Scaling Factor Approach for bolt-on valuation through software implementation, methodological relaxation of core assumptions, and simulation-based sample size determination to support broader adoption and standardization of bolt-on value set development.

Skin irritation and self-confidence bolt-ons show good content validity in atopic dermatitis and chronic urticaria, with skin irritation being the most important dimension for the majority of participants.

age_group: 8-15 years old (valued by adults for a 10-year-old child)
key_finding: The Brazilian EQ-5D-Y-3L value set was successfully developed using DCE and cTTO methods, with pain/discomfort identified as the most important domain and utility values ranging from 1.0 (full health) to -0.0059 (worst health state).

Joint modelling of health and time preference heterogeneity in DCE with duration valuation studies can improve value set derivation through flexible covariance specifications and optimized anchoring tasks.

The EQ-HWB-9 demonstrates acceptable validity, reliability, and discriminatory ability among informal caregivers with lower ceiling effects than EQ-5D-5L, supporting its use for capturing broader caregiver well-being.

Twelve quality of life dimensions were identified across five broader QoL measures and EQ-5D, with varying associations to self-reported health and wellbeing, suggesting the need for comprehensive multi-dimensional instruments or instrument suites.

This exploratory study tests the feasibility and performance of lag-time TTO as a valuation method for EQ-TIPS health states to inform selection of appropriate valuation methods for this new instrument.
A symposium and workshop were organized to inform healthcare decision makers and researchers about the Malaysian EQ-5D-5L value set and its applications in economic evaluations and outcomes research.

age_group: children and adolescents visiting PAWS clinic
key_finding: This project aims to develop a localized Form-SG powered EQ-5D-Y-5L questionnaire, establish age thresholds for self-report versus proxy completion in children with mental health conditions, and assess comparability between EQ-5D-Y-5L and EQ-5D-5L for transition to adult instruments.
This study compares EQ-5D-5L to well-being and capability measures in older adults to examine whether EQ-5D captures 'beyond health' domains relevant to social care.

This study evaluates the psychometric performance of eleven bolt-ons for the EQ-5D-5L in older adults to determine their potential to enhance health outcome measurement sensitivity in this population.

The new UK EQ-5D-5L value set yields higher utility scores for less severe health states and lower scores for severe states compared to the 5L-to-3L crosswalk, with larger differences observed in females and older respondents.
EQ-5D-5L with 'today' recall period performs reliably for stable chronic diseases but underestimates disease burden in episodic conditions with fluctuating symptoms.

age_group: various patient subgroups with specific ages
key_finding: The EQ-5D-5L improves predictions of unplanned hospital readmission within 1 year when added to administrative data models, with performance evaluated across patient subgroups stratified by age, clinical diagnosis, and neighborhood income.

age_group: older adults and ethnic minority populations
key_finding: Psychometric evaluation and cultural validation of EQ-HWB and EQ-5D instruments in Chinese populations, including ethnic minorities and long COVID patients.
Prospective observational study collecting EQ-5D-5L health states and utility values in French IBD patients to compare with disease-specific quality of life measures.
Cognition bolt-on items, particularly compound items covering calculation and learning, improved the psychometric performance of EQ-5D-5L in a Chinese elderly population.
Development of an EQ-5D-5L value set for the Mexican general population to support health technology assessment and health care quality monitoring.

EQ-5D research has expanded significantly across Latin America with multiple valuation studies and national population surveys, but knowledge gaps remain regarding proper implementation based on scientific evidence.

This study will provide the first systematic comparison of the EQ-HWB with widely used subjective wellbeing instruments to advance EQ-HWB from experimental to approved status and enhance comparability of quality-of-life evidence across health and wellbeing sectors.

This protocol development study aims to create a global survey instrument to assess HTA agencies' preferences and unmet needs regarding health utility data collection and use for reimbursement decision-making.

This study will examine the feasibility, validity, and responsiveness of the EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in measuring health-related quality of life in paediatric patients with congenital heart disease in China and compare their psychometric properties with PedsQL.

Three distinct preference classes were identified in Peruvian health valuation data, with quality-of-life oriented, length-of-life oriented, and middle classes showing substantially different EQ-5D-5L value sets, demonstrating significant preference heterogeneity within a national population.

This study examines whether the placement of EQ-5D bolt-on items relative to the EQ VAS affects EQ VAS scores to inform standardized sequencing recommendations for the EQ-5D Bolt-on Toolbox user guide.

This study assesses the content validity, comprehensibility, and cultural appropriateness of EQ-5D-5L cognition bolt-on items and EQ-HWB-S in Indonesian patients with schizophrenia, caregivers, and healthcare professionals.

Simultaneous control for heteroskedasticity and preference heterogeneity in health valuation produces consistent EQ-5D-5L value sets comparable to original studies, with scale adjustment improving model fit for respondents with lower preference intensity.
This project explores and assesses four methodological approaches to generate consistent utilities and QALYs across the life-course when different EQ instruments are used at different ages.

The choice of child perspective versus individual perspective for EQ-5D-Y health state valuation has significant normative and practical implications for value set development and economic evaluations in pediatric healthcare.

Psychological distance dimensions (social, temporal, spatial, hypothetical) explain differences in EQ-5D-Y utilities between child and adult perspectives, with higher psychological distance increasing mean utilities and reducing variance.
Comparison of health preferences across 11 Asian regions using standardized DCE data from EQ-5D-5L valuation studies to identify preference heterogeneity independent of methodological differences.
Both self-complete and proxy versions of EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrated validity, reliability, and responsiveness in Chinese children with leukemia, asthma, and school-attending populations.

The EQ-5D-5L requires modifications to improve face validity and appropriateness for Indigenous people in Canada, including consideration of colonial context and potential shifts to strength-based wording.
First study evaluating the psychometric performance of the EQ-5D-5L in Australian informal carers to assess validity of generic preference-based measures for use in this population.

This project investigates whether visually enhanced anchoring vignettes reduce reporting heterogeneity in EQ-5D and EQ-VAS responses by improving validity of vignette equivalence and response consistency assumptions.
A comprehensive methodological guide for analysing and reporting EQ-5D data was published as an open-access book to provide standardized approaches for researchers using EQ-5D instruments.

This study evaluates the feasibility, validity, reliability, and responsiveness of EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S in aged care settings across three Asian countries to determine their suitability for assessing health and well-being in older adults.
Workshop panel discussion comparing culture-specific preference-based measures (CHROM-G, AP-7D) versus generic EQ-5D for use in Asian populations.

Evaluation of content validity and psychometric properties of EQ-5D cognition bolt-on items in Parkinson's disease patients and caregivers to inform final selection of cognition bolt-ons for the EQ-5D.
Development of EQ-5D-5L value set for the Indian general population using hybrid modeling approach combining composite time trade-off and discrete choice experiment data.
Development of a theoretical framework and frequentist estimation methods for hybrid models combining TTO and DCE data for EQ-5D valuation while accounting for intra-person correlation.

Addition of a respiratory bolt-on dimension to the EQ-5D-5L showed small improvements in discriminant validity and correlation with COPD parameters, but with trade-offs in cross-disease comparability.
Development of a Kenya-specific QALY value set using EQ-5D-5L to enhance the validity of cost-effectiveness analyses and healthcare resource allocation decisions in Kenya.
Comparison of EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L value sets to assess whether the 5L version is more sensitive to changes in health status following total knee arthroplasty.

age_group: mixed ages with quotas set by age
key_finding: This study explores the feasibility of using the EQ-VT program for EQ-5D-5L valuation in rural China, addressing urban-rural disparities in computer access.
Educational session on EQ-5D-5L valuation presented at the Health Economics Study Group UK conference.

The EQ-5D-5L is being developed as the new reference instrument for valuation in France due to its improved sensitivity in capturing health-related quality of life variations compared to the EQ-5D-3L.

age_group: adults valuing health states for 10-year-old children
key_finding: Different perspectives in EQ-5D-Y valuation (individual vs. proxy, child vs. adult health states) produce systematic differences in valuations, with effects varying by health state severity and valuation method.
The study investigated the optimal degree of overlap and impact of color coding in discrete choice experiments to improve data quality.
EQ-DAPHNIE provides infrastructure for collecting and storing population health measurement data using EQ instruments across multiple countries to support future EuroQol research.

All 19 DCE designs tested were able to recover parameters, but no single set of design features consistently produced superior models across key indicators, suggesting trade-offs in design choices for EQ-5D-5L valuation studies.

This study assesses psychometric properties of EQ-HWB-9 modifications using a one-at-a-time testing approach to isolate the impact of each proposed change on item wording, response levels, and ordering.
A hybrid BWS-VAS approach is proposed to directly derive impact weights on the full health-dead scale for EQ-5D-5L valuation, potentially reducing cognitive burden compared to existing methods.
Large language models can be utilized to enhance patient-reported outcome measures including the EQ-5D and its bolt-on dimensions.
Travel grant to support presentation at the 16th IAHPR Meeting during an EuroQol-sponsored session.
TTO values exhibit end-aversion bias across all comparisons rather than only at full health, suggesting a contrasting effect that may warrant rescaling of preference values.
Logical inconsistency in TTO valuation data is substantially lower in China than England, explaining why Chinese EQ-5D-5L value sets show consistent level ordering while other countries do not.
statistical_methods: inconsistency measures (dummy variable, rate, distance, size, adjusted score)

key_finding: Development of hyreg2 R package enabling latent class estimation of EQ-5D-5L value sets using hybrid modeling with extended methodological capabilities including heteroscedasticity modeling and partial coefficients.
New evidence on interpretation, responsiveness, and cross-regional comparability of EQ-5D outcomes was disseminated at ISPOR Europe 2025.
EQ-HWB-9 shows promise for proxy use in people living with dementia but faces challenges with recall periods, proxy interpretation, and caregiver confidence in response selection.
First EQ-5D-3L population norms for Chile derived from the 2016-2017 National Health Survey, revealing lower EQ-5D VAS scores compared to other Latin American countries.

A hybrid scoring model combining formative and reflective approaches is suggested for the EQ-5D-5L in non-economic applications, as neither purely reflective nor formative approaches adequately address problematic dimensions like anxiety/depression and self-care.

age_group: community sample stratified by gender and age group composition
key_finding: AHP demonstrated comparable predictive ability to DCE for EQ-5D-5L health state valuation while imposing lower cognitive burden and being perceived as easier to understand and more preferred by respondents.

Country-related differential item functioning in EQ-5D-5L is minimal among linguistically similar countries but meaningful across different linguistic and cultural contexts, particularly in mobility, self-care, and usual activities dimensions.

EQ-5D-Y-3L value sets were successfully generated for four Asian countries using a hybrid latent class modelling approach, with worst health state values ranging from -0.198 to -0.582 across countries.

Distribution-based metrics (IQR, pits state value) better explain variability in EQ-5D-5L value sets than mean alone, and methodological shifts toward hybrid valuation and advanced modelling are improving comparability across regions.
Three studies assessed psychometric performance and validity of EQ-TIPS v2.0 in stunted children and EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB-9 in obese patients with and without bariatric surgery.

age_group: mixed (adults valuing adult and child perspectives)
key_finding: Subjects adopting a child perspective consistently gave higher TTO valuations than those adopting an adult perspective, with significant differences also observed between EQ-5D and EQ-5D-Y instruments.

age_group: across age groups including children and adults
key_finding: This systematic review investigates whether constant proportionality assumptions in health preference valuation hold empirically and how deviations from linear utility affect EQ-5D value set derivation across different populations and perspectives.

age_group: 65 years and over, with different age subgroups
key_finding: This study investigates face and content validity of the EQ-5D-5L in older people and explores their assessment of bolt-on dimensions when presented alongside the EQ-5D-5L.
Development of an EQ-5D-5L value set for the Brazilian population using composite time-trade-off and discrete choice experiment methods to support health economic evaluations.

The valueSetCompare R package provides a standardized framework for comparing HRQoL value sets, with EQ-5D-5L demonstrating greater sensitivity to severity changes and stronger interval measurement properties compared to EQ-5D-3L across 15 countries.
Parametric survival models can accommodate the asymmetric, heteroscedastic, and censored nature of cTTO data better than standard Tobit models used in EQ-5D-5L valuation studies.
Interval TTO (iTTO) reduces cognitive burden and improves task comprehension compared to composite TTO while maintaining equivalent model precision for EQ-5D-5L health state valuations.
EQ-HWB-9 demonstrates acceptable psychometric performance among informal caregivers with lower ceiling effects than EQ-5D-5L and captures broader wellbeing domains beyond health status.

age_group: adults and adolescents; tasks framed from perspective of 10-year-old child
key_finding: Comparison of DCE with duration split triplets and cTTO methods for valuing EQ-5D-Y-5L health states in Canada, with qualitative exploration of respondent decision-making processes.
To document whether specific cardiovascular complications arise after significant COVID-19 infection requiring hospital admission using 6-month outcome data including EQ-5D/EQ-VAS.

Evaluate the validity and responsiveness of the EQ-5D-5L Anxiety/Depression dimension over time in cancer patients with emotional distress using longitudinal IRT models and comparison with HADS and PHQ-4.

Health state valuations should account for duration and sequence effects rather than assuming values are independent of temporal context, with implications for QALY calculations and cost-effectiveness analyses.
To assess the dimensional coverage of EQ-5D in dementia and explore differences between self-reported and proxy-reported HRQoL data to inform bolt-on selection.
Development of a national EQ-5D-5L value set for Kazakhstan to support health technology assessment and economic evaluations using TTO and DCE methodologies.
This study evaluates the psychometric properties of EQ-TIPS in infants and toddlers with cerebral palsy in China to strengthen evidence for its adoption as an official instrument.

This study aims to translate and validate the EQ-TIPS for Hungarian caregivers of young children with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, and to explore factors affecting proxy reporting differences between caregiver dyads.

Over 50% of formerly hospitalized COVID-19 patients and 40% of non-hospitalized patients met criteria for post-COVID condition at 24 months, with significant associations with reduced health-related quality of life.

The OPUF method is feasible for creating value sets for the EQ-HWB-S even with smaller sample sizes, but requires further development to improve individual-level reliability and validity of preference weights.

Interviewer training on EQ-5D significantly reduces ceiling effects in face-to-face population surveys, and EQ-5D-5L demonstrates superior psychometric performance compared to EQ-5D-3L in reducing ceiling effects and improving discriminatory power in Chinese general populations.

A conceptual framework for measuring health-related quality of life in very young children should incorporate proxy responses and observational measures, with consideration for developmental stages across age groups 0-2, 2-3, and 4-5 years.
A value set for the EQ-5D-5L was successfully derived for the United Arab Emirates general population using a hybrid model approach.

A research visit to facilitate collaborative working on routine PROM data collection and analysis in the Canadian healthcare system and promote knowledge exchange between Canadian policymakers and UK experts.
Investigation of how EQ-5D utilities can capture severity concepts for healthcare priority setting and whether respondents prioritize the severely ill versus utility maximization.

age_group: parents and general adults (valuing health states for children aged 0-3 years)
key_finding: This study will assess the feasibility of applying latent discrete choice experiment methods to EQ-TIPS-5L valuation and identify which respondent groups and perspectives yield the most logically consistent preferences.

To culturally adapt and psychometrically validate EQ-TIPS for Indonesian infants and toddlers while quantifying caregiver spillover effects by linking child health-related quality of life with caregiver well-being.

A dissemination seminar in Bangladesh presented newly developed EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L value sets and piloting results of EQ-5D-Y to stakeholders including health ministry representatives, HTA bodies, researchers, and media to promote practical applicability for health technology assessment.
Development of a single sleep bolt-on item for the EQ-5D-5L through a sequential mixed methods approach to improve measurement sensitivity in populations with sleep problems.
An adapted EQ-5D-Y for children aged 2-4 years demonstrated improved sensitivity, validity, and reliability compared to the original EQ-5D-Y instrument.
Development and validation of a copula-based algorithm to transport aggregated EQ-5D utility values between value sets when individual patient data are unavailable.

A Brazilian EQ-5D-Y-3L value set was successfully developed with pain/discomfort identified as the most influential dimension, and EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrated good construct and known-group validity in children and adolescents.

A workshop introducing EuroQol instruments and their applications in healthcare decision-making across the MENA region, with focus on integrating EQ-5D into cost-utility analysis, value-based healthcare, and population health monitoring.

This study aims to translate the EQ-HWB-9 and three EQ-5D bolt-on dimensions (sleep, cognition, fatigue) into Standard Arabic with cognitive debriefing to ensure cultural and conceptual equivalence for use across Arabic-speaking populations.

Post-COVID syndrome participants had the poorest health-related quality of life and mental well-being, while government restriction stringency was associated with worsened mental well-being but improved anxiety/depression, with differential impacts between those with and without chronic conditions.

This project measures and decomposes socioeconomic inequalities in EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L using concentration index-based methods to determine how different CI variants respond to inequalities measured by EuroQol instruments.

This project develops standardised guidance for qualitative content validity testing of EQ-5D bolt-on dimensions to ensure high-quality data, enable resource sharing, and facilitate synthesis across studies.

countries: Multiple Countries (37 Total, Not Individually Specified)
key_finding: This systematic review examines ceiling effects of EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L in general adult populations and identifies factors influencing these effects across 94 studies from 37 countries.
EQ-5D proxy assessment in residential care facilities shows inconsistent construct validity and limited responsiveness evidence, with proxy-resident agreement ranging from poor to moderate.

Regional transformation functions may be used to convert DCE-derived latent utilities to TTO-derived health utilities, though global functions are not recommended due to variation between western and eastern countries.

Adding four bolt-ons (Skin Irritation, Self-confidence, Social Relationships, and Sleep) to EQ-5D-5L improved responsiveness to smaller health changes while maintaining good test-retest reliability in psoriasis and atopic dermatitis patients.
statistical_methods: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve

key_finding: Panel debate to discuss controversies around QALY-based HTA, cost-effectiveness thresholds, and EQ-5D recommendations with stakeholders from industry, HTA, academia, and EuroQol.
The EQ-5D-Y-3L is relevant for assessing HRQOL in Chinese children and adolescents but requires improvements in social health coverage, mental health dimension specificity, and question clarity.

This study examines the psychometric performance of the EQ-5D-5L in hospitalised older adults using routinely collected PROMs data to assess its validity, reliability, and responsiveness in this population.
This study aims to compare EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L responsiveness in rheumatology patients and develop a mapping function to enable comparability between historical 3L data and newly collected 5L data.

Significant differences in protocol adherence were observed between interviewers conducting composite time trade-off interviews for EQ-5D-5L valuation, with experienced interviewers generally following the protocol more closely than novice interviewers.

The EQ-5D-5L demonstrated good test-retest reliability, small to moderate responsiveness, and ability to discriminate between different health status levels in Ethiopian cervical cancer patients, with group-level MCID estimates of 0.10-0.15 for the index score.
Development of EQ-5D-5L value set for Nepal and direct comparison of DCEd versus cTTO valuation methods in a lower-middle-income country setting.

The EQ-5D-Y-5L is a psychometrically valid and feasible patient-reported outcome measure for use in routine paediatric clinical care, with strong acceptability among patients, caregivers, and clinicians when implemented with appropriate supports.
The EQ-5D-5L demonstrated robust measurement properties in Chinese patients with NSCLC, with performance comparable to SF-6D though with a higher ceiling effect.

The EQ-5D-5L outperformed the EQ-5D-3L for assessing health inequalities in general population samples, showing larger contrasts and lower ceiling effects, though both instruments are suitable for inequality analysis.

age_group: 5-15 years, with adolescent subgroup for valuation
key_finding: This project aims to develop EQ-5D-Y value sets for Ethiopia and compare measurement properties and valuations across child self-report, proxy, and adolescent perspectives.
This project aims to develop and psychometrically validate vision and cognition bolt-on descriptors for the EQ-5D-5L using qualitative and quantitative methods in the UK and Australia.

EQ-5D-5L metrics provide additional patient-perceived health status information beyond clinical outcomes and disease-specific PROMs in value-based healthcare settings, with disease-specific outcomes explaining more variance in EQ metrics than clinical indicators alone.

EQ-5D demonstrates meaningful performance as an indicator of socioeconomic inequalities, public health impacts, and quality of care in orthopedic surgery, with comparable measurement properties between adult and youth versions in adolescent populations.

This study aims to understand the measurement properties and transitions between EQ-5D-Y-3L, EQ-5D-Y-5L, and EQ-5D-5L among Chinese adolescents to address ceiling effects and provide guidance on instrument use across the lifespan.

age_group: 0-59 months (infants and toddlers), with subgroups: 0-12 months, 13-24 months, 24-36 months, 36-59 months
key_finding: This study aims to translate, culturally adapt, and validate the Bangla version of EQ-TIPS for infants and toddlers aged 2-4 years in Bangladesh, assessing psychometric properties including feasibility, reliability, validity, and responsiveness in both healthy and ill children.

Although 86 methods for measuring time preference exist across disciplines, no method has both theoretically sound characteristics and feasibility for online self-completion in EQ-5D valuation studies.

age_group: adults valuing health states for themselves and for 10-year-old children
key_finding: Wording of the descriptive system (EQ-5D-3L vs EQ-5D-Y) and perspective (adult vs child) interact to influence health state valuations, with the lowest utilities for the worst health state observed in the EQ-5D-3L adult perspective condition.
EQ-5D-5L health state valuations differ when framed within a palliative care context, with factors like limited life expectancy and support levels influencing valuations.

An EQ-5D-based patient decision aid may improve decision quality and reduce decisional regret in individuals considering bariatric surgery by incorporating both clinical benefits and health-related quality of life outcomes.

Ordinal preference structures between cTTO and DCE data show inadequate agreement (κ=0.35), with agreement worsening as health state proximity decreases, suggesting these methods are not commensurable for hybrid valuation approaches.

The Interviewer-Administered EQ-5D-5L version demonstrates high agreement with self-complete modes at the dimension level and is a viable alternative for populations with limited literacy or physical constraints, though EQ-VAS and utility scores show greater variability across populations.
Paper and electronic versions (handheld, tablet, web, IVR) of the EQ-5D-5L produce equivalent data with negligible differences in mean scores and high correlations at the group level.

DCE and TTO coefficients show moderate agreement on individual level (mean Pearson r=0.435) but strong agreement on aggregate level (r=0.871-0.906), with better consistency among respondents with higher quality DCE data.

Random-effects regression models with M2 terms (capturing mild problems in 1-2 dimensions) best predict EQ-5D-5L TTO values in China, suggesting Chinese populations rate mildest health states differently than other populations.
Post-doctoral training project focused on research proposal writing and manuscript development related to EQ-5D, though specific research outcomes were not prioritized for publication.

age_group: mixed ages including younger and lower-income residents
key_finding: Six studies collectively advance EQ-5D measurement, valuation, and application by examining population health trends, clinical outcomes, health economic evaluation, value set availability, and cross-national variation in utility values.
This study aims to develop a country-specific EQ-5D-Y-3L value set for Belgium using DCE and TTO methods, and to assess whether health preferences differ between children and adolescents.

Two specialized workshops in China successfully promoted understanding and adoption of EQ-5D instruments among diverse stakeholders including researchers, clinicians, pharmacists, and industry representatives.
Neither proxy version of EQ-5D-Y-3L nor EQ-5D-Y-5L demonstrated clear superiority, with assessment perspective not significantly affecting proxy-reported HRQoL in children with asthma or eczema.
This project examines the psychometric properties, responsiveness, and scoring approaches of the EQ-5D-5L psoriasis bolt-on to support its advancement to approved EuroQol instrument status.

This study aims to develop and test Dimension Specific Modules (DSMs) using EuroQol-owned instruments and items, specifically exploring cognition as a bolt-on construct through combined classical psychometric and modern test theory approaches.

age_group: children aged 2-18 years and their carers
key_finding: This study aims to conduct detailed psychometric analysis of EuroQol instruments in children and carers, develop a crosswalk between EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L, and establish an international protocol for psychometric testing of EuroQol measures.

age_group: mixed, with particular focus on younger age groups (females <40 years)
key_finding: While EQ-5D is commonly used in long COVID research, there is limited evidence of its psychometric properties in this condition, with considerable heterogeneity across long COVID populations and greater HRQoL burden in females aged under 40 years.

Recall periods affect EQ-HWB-9 more than EQ-5D-5L with small overall effects, and 'last week' versions perform slightly better in the general population, with EQ-HWB VAS demonstrating validity and capturing distinct concepts from EQ VAS.

Development of a mixed logit model estimation tool in R that enables efficient analysis of DCE data with duration components while accommodating non-linear time preferences for QALY tariff derivation.
Analysis of how socioeconomic inequalities in health-related quality of life change across the life course and which EQ-5D dimensions contribute most to overall health inequality.
Mobility is perceived as the most important health dimension in Uzbekistan, with age and health experiences as strong predictors of self-reported health on the EQ-VAS scale.

age_group: 15 adult patients and 15 children and adolescent patients
key_finding: EQ-5D-5L and EQ-5D-Y capture most aspects of quality of life in DMD patients but may lack social relationship components and have limited appropriateness for physical health items in this population.
The EQ-PSO bolt-on dimensions for itching and self-confidence improve content validity and better reflect the lived experience of patients with psoriasis compared to the standard EQ-5D-5L alone.
COVID-19 lockdown in Spain resulted in a 32% increase in anxiety/depression problems and an estimated loss of 60,520 QALYs over 21 days in the general population.
Further validation of EQ-HWB/EQ-HWB-S as standalone measures is needed to address item comprehension challenges that may be influenced by surrounding content in qualitative interviews or surveys.
Create a standardized database archive of EQ-5D-5L general population survey data to generate population norms and inequality indicators across multiple countries.

Longer recall timeframes with intensity or frequency response scales improve EQ-5D-5L's psychometric properties in obstructive airway disease patients by reducing ceiling effects and improving reliability and responsiveness.

Differences between UK 3L and English 5L value sets are primarily caused by differences in underlying preference data rather than modelling methods, though modelling approaches have greater impact on 5L values.
Comparative assessment of the reliability, validity, and usefulness of EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L versions in epilepsy patients in a low-income setting, including content validity investigation.

Both Tigrinya versions of EQ-5D-Y (3L and 5L) demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties with EQ-5D-Y-5L showing higher discriminative power, though ceiling effects were more pronounced in the 3L version.

age_group: older adults in residential care facilities
key_finding: This study evaluates whether the 25-item EQ-HWB provides added measurement value over the 9-item EQ-HWB-S in UK care home settings and assesses its psychometric performance and feasibility in this population.

This study explores whether decision-making processes captured by cumulative prospect theory parameters in TTO valuation are reflected in actual TTO responses using mouse tracking to measure attention allocation.

The EQ-VAS is interpreted differently across general public and clinical populations in Ethiopia, with the general public finding it challenging due to lack of scale explanations, while those with health conditions find it straightforward and suggest hash marks at 5- or 10-point intervals to represent meaningful change.

Standardized methodology for reporting EQ-5D-5L population norms and health inequalities was successfully established and demonstrated using English and Spanish general population survey data, showing robust evidence of socioeconomic inequalities in health across both countries.
This study investigates the actual reference period trauma patients use when responding to the EQ-5D's 'your health today' question and whether rapid health fluctuations affect their interpretation.
Both EQ-TIPS-3L and EQ-TIPS-5L demonstrated good content and construct validity, as well as responsiveness to recovery, for assessing health-related quality of life in acutely ill young children.

age_group: 6 age-specific groups across adult lifespan, with focus on older adults
