key_finding: This secondary data analysis examined the convergent validity and dimensionality of component items within self-care, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression dimensions across age groups to inform development of deep-dive modules.

age_group: older adults, community-dwelling and in assistive living environments
key_finding: This study evaluates the content validity of the EQ-HWB-S and EQ-5D-5L with five bolt-ons to identify which instruments best capture health-related quality of life and well-being domains important to older adults.
Narrative descriptions of EQ-5D-5L health states may reduce time preference distortion in lead-time TTO valuation by decreasing perceived temporal distance.
Development of a Thai EQ-5D-Y value set for children aged 8-15 years to enable accurate utility assessment and cost-utility analysis in pediatric health technology assessment.

This study aims to explore recall bias in retrospective EQ-5D-5L and bolt-on measurements among post-COVID-19 condition patients and assess how coping mechanisms influence health domain reporting and contribute to measurement bias.

This scoping review aims to identify contemporary qualitative studies assessing content validity in generic preference-weighted measures including EQ instruments and map current practice against existing guidance to identify good practice examples and methodological gaps.

Adult involvement in EQ-5D-Y valuation lacks empirical support for the taxpayer argument and requires greater conceptual clarity about the normative roles adults should take in valuing child health-related quality of life.

Create a comprehensive international database of EQ-5D-5L population norms and health inequality indicators from general population surveys across multiple countries to support comparative health outcomes research.

This study investigates whether itching and fatigue are adequately captured by the EQ-5D-5L pain/discomfort dimension or require bolt-on status, and develops a standard approach for evaluating bolt-on necessity in burn patients.

This PhD project will develop and test methods to identify and correct reporting heterogeneity in EuroQol instruments using vignettes, and explore whether differences in health knowledge and beliefs are sources of such heterogeneity.
Validation of self and proxy ratings of the global cognition bolt-on for EQ-5D-5L in patients with Alzheimer's Disease and related dementias.

Despite significant mean differences between directly reported and recalled EQ-5D-5L and EQ-VAS scores, high ICCs indicate good relative agreement, suggesting recalled scores are suitable for retrospective group-level analyses but not for individual-level use.
An EQ-5D-5L value set was successfully derived based on Uruguayan population preferences using time trade-off methodology.

This project aims to explore the relationship between EQ-5D-5L items and Work Disability Functional Assessment Battery item banks to inform the development of dimension-specific modules and compare two conceptual frameworks of health-related quality of life.

EQ-5D-Y-3L and -5L are feasible and valid instruments for assessing health-related quality of life in children and adolescents with ADHD, with EQ-5D-Y-5L showing superior discriminative validity between ADHD and general population groups.
A pluralistic approach to EQ-5D-Y-5L valuation may be needed to accommodate varying social value judgements and priority setting principles across different jurisdictions.
This study aims to assess HRQoL changes during transition from pediatric to adult care in adolescents with complex health conditions and validate EQ-5D-5L sensitivity in this population.
EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L demonstrate sufficient construct validity and responsiveness in upper respiratory tract diseases, particularly chronic rhinosinusitis and allergic rhinitis.

This study evaluates alternative item versions for the EQ-HWB long form, focusing on negatively versus positively phrased items and the inclusion of 'use of aids' references for vision and hearing items.

age_group: adolescents (10 years old) and adults (20 years old) as hypothetical perspectives; respondents of unspecified age
key_finding: Higher TTO utilities for hypothetical children versus adults' own health are not driven by adolescent years receiving greater weight on health or survival, but rather by the shift from self- to other-perspective.

age_group: children aged 0-3 years (proxy respondents are US adults); child ages tested: 1, 2, 3, and 4 years
key_finding: This exploratory study will test the relevance and consistency of EQ-TIPS attributes across child ages and task designs to inform preference-based valuation of the instrument for toddlers and infants.

age_group: adults valuing health states for children and themselves
key_finding: Duration, religious beliefs, and attitudes toward euthanasia significantly influence whether severe EQ-5D-Y-3L health states are valued as better than dead or worse than dead across self and proxy perspectives.

This project aims to demonstrate the clinical value of EQ-5D-5L for individual patient-level decision support through optimized display formats and predictive models across multiple chronic conditions.

The EQ-HWB-9 demonstrates good overall comprehensibility across four languages but requires refinement of frequency qualifiers, double-barrelled items, and language-specific terminology to strengthen cross-cultural validity.

EQ-5D-5L is feasible and acceptable among disabled Ethiopians but requires incorporation of additional dimensions (vision, hearing, social interaction) to better reflect health experiences of people with disabilities in low-income settings.

Investigation of the psychometric properties, feasibility and usefulness of the EQ-5D-Y when used to monitor health-related quality of life in children with chronic illness across different institutional contexts.
To evaluate the psychometric properties of the EQ-5D-5L vision bolt-on in patients with type 2 diabetes and controls to support its inclusion in the EQ-5D Bolt-on Toolbox.
A national EQ-5D-3L value set was successfully developed for Jordan using cTTO and DCE data, with mobility impairment showing the highest utility decrement.

This longitudinal study aims to generate representative HRQoL data from Egypt's general adult population to enhance global representativeness of the EQ-DAPHNIE initiative and facilitate cross-country comparisons.
Direct use of discrete choice experiments is feasible among Canadian adolescents aged 13-18 years, with minor presentation and framing issues that could be improved for future valuation studies.
Routine collection of quality of life data using EuroQol instruments is feasible in residential aged care facilities, with EQ-5D-5L and EQ-HWB demonstrating good performance and acceptability.

This study compares three modes of administration (interview-based, unsupervised virtual classroom, unsupervised online) for DCE with duration valuation studies using EQ-5D-5L and develops quality control measures for interviewer-administered data collection.

A novel calibration method for discrete choice experiments that anchors health states and the localization of 'dead' together produces logically ordered coefficients and health-state values unbiased by respondent difficulty with appraising the 'dead' state.

This study examines the validity, conceptual overlap, and psychometric properties of the EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S compared to other preference-based wellbeing measures (ICECAP-A, ASCOT, WiX) in the general Australian population.
This research explores how recall bias, reference frames, response styles, and life events affect the validity and comparability of EQ-5D-5L data in longitudinal population health studies.

age_group: representative of Canary Islands population in terms of age and gender
key_finding: Reintroducing a ranking task prior to composite TTO valuation did not significantly reduce inconsistencies or improve data quality in EQ-5D valuation studies.
statistical_methods: comparison of inconsistency rates across study arms

key_finding: International dissemination of EQ-HWB research through conference presentation and academic exchange facilitated methodological refinement for preference elicitation and longitudinal study design in elderly rehabilitation care.

The decomposed anxiety/depression dimensions of the EQ-5D-5L demonstrate superior psychometric performance compared to the composite dimension, with better convergent validity and known-group validity.
DCE surveys for EQ-5D valuation show significant sequence effects and heuristic biases including magnification, position bias, and lexicographic preferences that vary by task difficulty order.

This qualitative study explores respondents' understanding of EQ-HWB VAS versions and positively/negatively framed items across four countries to inform instrument development decisions regarding item polarity and VAS conceptualization.

age_group: undergraduate students and general population across age groups (quota sampling by age)
key_finding: Non-iterative TTO variants (nTTO and oTTO) demonstrated feasibility advantages over cTTO with reduced administration time, though cTTO showed superior modelling performance; rural populations in China valued health states significantly lower than urban populations.
statistical_methods: main effects model with interaction terms

key_finding: The study investigates whether the generic EQ-5D-Y demonstrates concurrent validity with the disease-specific JAMAR in children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, potentially enabling its use as a brief HRQoL screening tool in clinical practice.
Psychometric comparison of experimental and modified versions of EQ-HWB-9 to support instrument finalization and provide evidence for key EuroQol markets.
Deriving EQ-5D-5L preference weights for Denmark using composite TTO and DCE methodology, with exploration of triplet DCE with duration as an extension to the standard EQ-VT protocol.
This study explores whether adolescents can successfully complete DCE, TTO, and DCE with duration valuation tasks for EQ-5D-Y-5L to inform the development of Ethiopia's value set.

Face and content validity testing of candidate EQ-5D items in Australia identified problematic wording in communication and hearing/speech items and suggested layout and clarification amendments for mobility and interaction items.
EQ-HWB demonstrates comparable performance to EQ-5D-5L for measuring health-related quality of life but shows greater sensitivity to mental disease burden and can discriminate caregiving burden.

Time trade-off follow-up questions reveal that discounting does not follow standard functional forms, fear of immediate death is equivalent to approximately 1.5 years in full health, and duration shortening increases acceptance of severe health states.
Collaborative engagement in health state valuation studies is significantly misaligned with best practice recommendations from health economics and patient-reported outcome literature.

The EQ-5D-Y-5L is comprehensible and has moderate concurrent validity for children with intellectual disability, but lacks comprehensiveness and may benefit from supplementary questions about communication, social engagement, and mental health.

The EQ-HWB-S demonstrated suitable psychometric performance for measuring health and wellbeing in representative Australian and New Zealand populations, with known-group validity and convergent validity supporting its use across general and caregiver populations.
A Stata command (eq5d5l) was successfully developed and validated to calculate country-specific EQ-5D-5L index values across 3,125 health states using 11 different country-specific value sets.

Development and piloting of qualitative research materials (interview guide, survey instrument, coding framework) to inform the creation of a fatigue bolt-on for the EQ-5D-5L in persons living with multiple sclerosis.

The EQ-HWB-S demonstrated superior convergent validity compared to EQ-5D-5L and ReQoL-UI when validated against the Kessler 6-item psychological distress measure in both general population and individuals with mental health problems.
Metastatic colorectal cancer patients showed reduced health-related quality of life (mean VAS 62.12) compared to the general population (mean VAS 85.15), with 70.68% having at least one comorbidity.

To develop a method for testing interactions between bolt-on dimensions and core EQ-5D-5L dimensions using lottery-based choices to determine whether combined health problems have additive or non-additive utility effects.

EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L Amharic versions demonstrated good agreement and acceptable psychometric performance (test-retest reliability ICC 0.62-0.80, known-group validity supported) across interviewer administration and proxy-report in school children aged 5-8 years.

EQ-5D-Y-3L demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties in children with phobias but less satisfactory properties in children with autism, with self-completed versions performing better than proxy versions.

This research program aims to address methodological issues concerning the inclusion of informal carer outcomes in health economic evaluation using the EQ-5D, including assessment of psychometric performance, extent of double-counting, and differential weighting of carer versus patient QALYs.
Evaluate the construct validity of breathing and cognition bolt-ons for the EQ-5D-5L in non-hospitalized COVID-19 patients to enhance the instrument's utility in respiratory and cognitive research.
International meeting to share experiences and discuss priorities for research and development in the use of EQ-5D as a patient-reported outcome measure in routine healthcare systems.

Educational outreach to Asian HTA practitioners on EQ-5D instruments, value sets, and new non-commercial licensing policies, with review of recent Asian research on EuroQol instruments and their appropriateness for use in Asian populations.

Evaluate the sensitivity, validity, and discriminative ability of the EQ-5D-Y-5L in measuring health-related quality of life among obese and non-obese US children, and assess its concurrent validity with established physical activity and sleep measures.

A co-designed protocol for developing an interviewer-guided O-PUF/CAPI approach was created to improve data quality and respondent understanding, particularly for older respondents and complex instruments like EQ-HWB.
Development of free R commands (hyreg and xreg) to make hybrid regression modelling more accessible for EQ-5D and general applications.

Self-reported health via EQ-5D-5L and incentives (cash or telephone nudges) did not significantly impact TB screening compliance in rural Ghana, likely because pop-up clinics reduced compliance costs.
Systematic review of minimally important difference estimations for EQ-5D across different components, methods, populations, and health states with critical appraisal of anchor-based approaches.

EQ-5D is sensitive to discriminate health-related quality of life between informal caregivers with different levels of care burden, with patient utility score and care burden being significant predictors across EQ-5D dimensions.

age_group: includes older adults and individuals with disabilities
key_finding: This study examines whether digital layout format (item-by-item vs. grid) affects data quality, response patterns, and construct validity of the EQ-HWB-9 across device types in Germany and Argentina.

Recall bias in retrospective pre-injury HRQL assessment is primarily random error at group level, but individual-level estimates may be substantially distorted, particularly in trauma subgroups with lower education, comorbidity, or PTSD symptoms.
EQ-5D-5L demonstrated similar or better measurement properties compared to EQ-5D-3L, with moderately better distributional parameters and substantial improvement in informativity.

Current methodologies for estimating Minimal Important Difference (MID) with EQ-5D lack standardization, with significant variations across patient groups and unclear guidance on appropriate application to descriptive systems versus indices.

Different framings of the worse-than-dead distinction in health state valuation yield substantially different results, with lead-time TTO and CUA-based frames producing 1.5- to 2.7-fold higher odds of classifying states as worse than dead compared to regular TTO.
This feasibility study assessed whether EQ-TIPS attributes and severity levels align with preferences and compared kaizen tasks versus paired comparisons for EQ-TIPS valuation in small samples.

This study generates the first nationally representative EQ-5D-Y-3L population reference data for Bangladeshi children and adolescents and compares the impact of applying different international value sets on utility scores.

Misspecification in EQ-5D-5L valuation studies is primarily dependent on sample size (optimal around 1000 respondents) and number of health states (80-120 states), with minimal impact from state selection strategy.
Development of the first nationally representative Turkish EQ-5D-5L value set using standardized EQ-VT protocol to enable health technology assessment and cross-national comparability.
EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S demonstrate comparable or superior measurement properties to EQ-5D-5L in the Italian general population, with EQ-HWB-S showing better discrimination for social care users.
The study aims to evaluate the psychometric properties of the EQ-5D-Y-5L and compare its performance with the EQ-5D-Y-3L for assessing mental health in children and adolescents in China.

Geographic variation exists in health state preferences across regions, with differences in the relationship between elicitation methods that have implications for health technology assessment decision-making.

EQ-5D-5L data collected through Workers' Compensation Board surveys will be used to assess the impact of RTW programs on injured workers' health-related quality of life and predict return-to-work outcomes.
A hybrid 8-parameter model combining composite time-trade-off and discrete choice experiment data was selected to develop the Malaysian EQ-5D-5L value set, with values ranging from -0.442 to 1.
This study evaluates the content validity and psychometric properties of EQ-HWB-S in patients with advanced illness to support person-centred end-of-life care and economic evaluations.
Bayesian D-efficient DCE designs that account for nonlinear time preferences outperform conventional DCE designs for estimating QALY tariffs unconfounded by respondent time preferences.

The EQ-5D-3L demonstrated greater acceptability than the MSIS-8D but lower informativity, and both measures showed limited responsiveness to disease-modifying treatment initiation in people with multiple sclerosis.

A geometric mean aggregation method for TTO utilities preserves relative preference inversion and independence of irrelevant alternatives properties, producing a narrower range of utilities compared to standard arithmetic averaging.

A taxonomy of value set redundancy has been developed to help EuroQol and policy makers identify when existing value sets require updating based on methodological, normative, population, and preference-based factors.

Removing the first sorting question from composite TTO improves sensitivity to health state severity for worse-than-dead states by establishing a statistically significant association between level sum score and utility values.
Symposium presenting challenges and opportunities in measuring and valuing health in children using EuroQol instruments.

This is a comprehensive impact assessment of EuroQol Research Foundation's activities over 2015-2025 to evaluate how its health measurement instruments and funded research have shaped clinical practice, health technology assessment, and policy decision-making globally.
The study assessed the use of a feedback module to model EQ-5D-5L health state values in Hong Kong.

The EQ-HWB-S is presented as a potential broader QALY measure for health technology assessment that extends beyond traditional health-related quality of life to include social care and wellbeing dimensions.

This feasibility study assessed the use of DCE with kaizen tasks as a practical valuation method for EQ-5D-5L bolt-on attributes, specifically examining cognition bolt-ons (composite and component versions) and their importance relative to core dimensions.

age_group: ≥18 years old, with focus on ≥65 years old (approximately 7,000 older adults)
key_finding: This study will identify measurement strengths and gaps of the EQ-5D-5L in older populations and recommend candidate bolt-on dimensions to improve sensitivity.

Extension of EQ-5D-5L value set data collection from England to other UK countries (Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland) to support UK-wide health technology assessment and value-based pricing decisions.

age_group: adolescents aged 12-17 years, with comparison to adults; also includes proxy valuation for 10-year-old
key_finding: This study will test the feasibility of nonlinear DCE valuation methods in adolescent samples and compare value sets between adolescents and adults to inform the EQ-5D-Y-5L valuation protocol.

This project aims to establish clinically meaningful thresholds for the EQ-5D-5L to enable screening for emotional distress in advanced melanoma patients and demonstrate the practicality of PROMs-based screening in routine clinical care.

Non-iterative TTO (NITTO) appears feasible as an alternative valuation method, with respondents finding it less cognitively challenging than DCETTO while maintaining logical consistency, though some health states show implausibly low values.

EQ-5D-5L and PROMIS-29 have substantial differences in their measurement and valuation properties that interact in complex ways and significantly impact QALY estimates depending on condition nature and severity.
A national conference to advance measurement and valuation of health outcomes across clinical practice and research, featuring methodological innovations in PROMs science and implementation.

This study aims to support item selection for a new health-related quality of life instrument (E-QALY) through psychometric analysis and IRT in Argentina, incorporating data on financial coping and patient/family costs across disease groups.

This study investigates the relationship between climate change exposure and psychological responses and their impact on health-related quality of life measured by EQ-5D-5L, and evaluates the known-group validity of EQ-5D-5L in differentiating between subgroups with varying levels of climate change exposure and psychological responses.

Four distinct viewpoints on quality of life were identified across patients, carers, and healthy general publics, with EQ-HWB items consistently rated as highly relevant across all groups, supporting the instrument's validity for diverse populations.
This pilot study tests the feasibility of a DCE-duration protocol for valuing the EQ-HWB-S and compares results with prior EQ-VT valuation to assess agreement between methods.

To explore how generic health-related quality of life instruments (EQ-5D-Y-5L and PedsQL) can be integrated into routine clinical care for paediatric patients with rare diseases through co-design with patients, carers, and clinicians.

age_group: adults valuing health states for a 10-year-old child
key_finding: A latent scale EQ-5D-Y value set was successfully developed using DCE with UK adults, with mixed logit models demonstrating superior fit compared to multinomial logit approaches.

This educational workshop promoted the use of EQ-5D instruments in the Indo-Pacific region and showcased capacity strengthening opportunities and applications in national health surveys, cohort studies, and electronic health records.

Discrete choice experiments with partial profile presentation of EQ-5D-5L health states produce significantly different parameter estimates compared to full profile presentation, with respondent inference of missing attributes not fully explaining the discrepancy.

age_group: newborns, parents, and siblings of preterm infants
key_finding: This longitudinal study will assess whether EuroQol instruments can capture health spillover effects on parents and siblings of babies with necrotising enterocolitis over neonatal discharge, 6 months, and 1 year follow-up.
A Nigerian-specific EQ-5D-5L value set was successfully developed from a representative population of adult Nigerians, with Pain/Discomfort identified as the most important dimension.

age_group: informal caregivers of elderly people with dementia
key_finding: Health literacy is a statistically significant predictor of health-related quality of life as measured by EQ-5D-5L among informal caregivers of persons with dementia.

This PhD will develop criteria and methods to generate EQ-5D-5L bolt-on value sets by conducting a scoping review, stakeholder interviews, and feasibility survey to address unique valuation challenges presented by extended EQ-5D-5L descriptive systems.

This study examines the psychometric properties of interviewer-administered EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in children aged 6-10 with orthopaedic conditions using official traditional Chinese (Hong Kong) versions.

This study evaluates measurement properties of three VAS construct versions (health, health and wellbeing, quality of life) paired with EQ-HWB-9 to determine which construct demonstrates optimal properties for potential inclusion with the EQ-HWB.
Empirical analysis of the EQ-5D Anxiety/Depression dimension to create a formal definition and derive a predictive algorithm based on GHQ-12 and WEMBS scores.

The study evaluated the psychometric properties of five bolt-on dimensions (skin irritation, self-confidence, social relationships, social participation, and feeling connected) added to the EQ-5D-5L in German patients with chronic inflammatory dermatological conditions.

This study examines the comparability and transition between EQ-5D-5L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in Chinese adolescents aged 12-18 years with atopic dermatitis or mental health problems by comparing response distributions and psychometric properties.

age_group: children and adolescents residing in orphanages
key_finding: This study aims to validate the EQ-5D-Y-3L and EQ-5D-Y-5L in vulnerable child populations in South Korea through cultural adaptation and psychometric evaluation, including a head-to-head comparison of both versions.

This study examines the comprehensibility and feasibility of self-complete and interviewer-assisted administration of EQ-5D-Y-5L and EQ-5D-Y-3L among younger children (6-10 years) with chronic illness to determine minimum age, optimal administration mode, and version suitability.

The modified Argentine Spanish version of the EQ-HWB-S demonstrates content validity for measuring health and wellbeing in patients, social care users, and informal caregivers, with appropriate comprehension of the frequency scale and questionnaire items.
Evaluation of the psychometric properties, feasibility, validity, and responsiveness of the EQ-5D-5L in critically ill sepsis patients during acute phase and longitudinal follow-up.
The Memory-Concentration cognition bolt-on module demonstrated superior psychometric performance and ceiling reduction compared to a composite cognition item, with minimal added response burden.
Experimental and modified EQ-HWB-9 versions showed comparable psychometric performance with some wording changes improving distributional properties and known-group validity.

A visit to King Saud University aimed at fostering EuroQol research collaboration, disseminating knowledge about EuroQol instruments and their applications, and establishing long-term partnerships between the EuroQol network and Saudi institutions.

Reference dependency exists in EQ-5D-5L valuations from general population respondents, with those in impaired health showing approximately 30% smaller health-state decrements, but this does not bias the resulting social tariff.

This study will evaluate the psychometric properties of cognition bolt-on items for the EQ-5D-5L in Chinese post-stroke patients to support their refinement and potential inclusion in the EuroQol Bolt-on Toolbox.

The EQ-HWB-S is expected to demonstrate superior psychometric validity and sensitivity compared to EQ-5D-5L in cancer surveillance populations due to its broader coverage of anxiety, control, and wellbeing dimensions.
To empirically test preference inversion between levels 4 and 5 of EQ-5D-5L items using paired comparisons in a nationally representative US sample.

Fuzzy set theory-derived concordance measures reveal asymmetric agreement between patient and proxy raters of EQ-5D-3L/VAS, with proxy agreement to patient health states stronger than vice versa in the acute phase but converging over time.
statistical_methods: fuzzy set operators (Zadeh, bounded sum, product)

key_finding: Multi-national content validity testing of EQ-TIPS led to key changes in the descriptive system, with Version 3.0 now undergoing psychometric validation testing.
Generation of a nationally representative EQ-5D-5L value set for Zambia to support health technology assessment and cost-effectiveness analysis in policy decisions.
Project disseminated findings from four distinct studies on EQ-5D and EQ-VAS outcomes across general populations and clinical contexts at international conferences.
First regional overview of health perceptions of Latin-American people using Gallup World Poll 2007-2008 data across 22 countries.

The EQ-HWB-9 performed well in meditation app users with mental health concerns, and reordering items to place the activities question first improved measurement properties by encouraging broader interpretation of activities.
Older adults with various disabilities found the digital prototype of EQ-HWB-9 easy to engage with and acceptable, with preferences identified for design refinements.

Public expectations about consequences of ill-health better explain VAS valuations than health state classifications alone, and the public systematically overestimates the impact of mobility and self-care problems while underestimating anxiety/depression effects compared to patient experiences.

Cross-cultural adaptation of EQ-TIPS into Chichewa identified challenges in translating emotional concepts (managing emotions, interacting with others, pain, sleep) and revealed that observable items were easier to translate than emotional items, with implications for other Bantu languages in sub-Saharan Africa.
To develop an Indonesian EQ-5D-5L value set and validate the instrument in the general population, impoverished families, and breast cancer patients.
Exploration of Visual Analogue Scale variations for measuring health, social care, and carer-related quality of life using mixed methods.
Derive a preference-based value set for the EQ-5D-5L from the Irish general population and examine variations in preferences across population groups.

age_group: patients mean age 40.07 years (SD=15.50), caregivers mean age 39.37 years (SD=12.90)
key_finding: Modified EQ-HWB-9 items demonstrated high comprehensibility and relevance in Indonesian cancer patients and caregivers, with clear preferences for activities-first ordering, shorter non-repeating stems, improved wording clarity, and modified frequency labels.
Educational short course on EQ-5D instruments for pharmacoeconomics professionals in South China.
A collaborative visit to advance EQ-5D-Y-5L valuation protocol development and strengthen organizational relationships within EuroQol and Erasmus University.

This study aims to disentangle whether non-additive preferences in EQ-5D valuations reflect genuine preference structures or boundary-induced compression by comparing interaction effects across cTTO and DCE valuation data from ten countries.

Adding a cognition dimension to the EQ-5D-3L increases explanatory power for health-related quality of life in injury patients, with cognitive problems showing comparable impact to other EQ-5D dimensions.

A PhD project examining the desirability, feasibility, and impact of involving children in the valuation of EQ-5D-Y health states, with exploration of child-appropriate valuation tasks and methods for meaningful child participation in health state valuation research.
Development of a new research grant on population norms for EQ-5D in older adults in Singapore.

The EQ-HWB and EQ-HWB-S were successfully translated into German following the researcher-led translation protocol, with constructs easily understood and well perceived by respondents in cognitive debriefing.

age_group: parents and caregivers of children aged 0-4 years
key_finding: Assessment of EQ-HWB-S's capacity to reflect spillover effects of children's health status on caregivers' health-related quality of life across five countries.
To compare how individuals rate hypothetical vignettes of health and wellbeing using the EQ VAS and alternative VAS versions to determine the most suitable VAS for adoption with the EQ-HWB-9.
A reduced orthogonal design of 25 health states performs comparably to the standard EQ-VT 86-state design for estimating EQ-5D-5L value sets, potentially reducing respondent burden.
Dissemination of EQ-HWB instrument to health outcomes professionals and instrument development experts at ISPOR Europe 2024.
Derivation of social value sets for the EQ-5D-5L in Peru using a lite protocol with DCE variants and hybrid modelling approaches.

EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L generate different utility values in cancer patients, with 3L tariffs producing larger health gains and more favorable cost-effectiveness ratios than 5L tariffs, particularly for large reductions in health-related quality of life.
A simulation laboratory was developed to enable testing of differences between EQ-5D-3L and EQ-5D-5L instruments in patient populations through profile and valuation data simulation.

This study aims to identify effective visualization formats of routinely collected EQ-5D data for health system administrators and decision-makers in hip and knee arthroplasty to promote uptake and use in Canadian health systems.

The new integrated interviewer-administered EQ-5D-5L version demonstrates acceptable comparability with existing face-to-face and telephone versions and may be used interchangeably, though individual-level substitution is not recommended due to limits of agreement.

Stage 3 testing of face validity for a new broad generic quality of life measure applicable across health, social care, and carer sectors in Argentina to assess translatability of language and concepts.
Testing face and content validity of EQ-HWB domains and items in Chinese population from Shanghai.
Respondents with chronic conditions preferred positively stated items and frequency-based response scales, with preferences guided by instrument context of use.
Development of an EQ-5D-Y-5L value-set for India to enable accurate health utility assessment and QALY estimation in pediatric health technology assessments using Indian population preferences.

Development of a user-friendly EQ-5D-5L utility index score calculator using the Egyptian value set to facilitate accurate and efficient calculation of health utility values for healthcare professionals and researchers.
Derive a scoring weight to convert Japanese EQ-5D-Y responses to index values using DCE and TTO valuation methods for cost-effectiveness analysis implementation.
The Amharic EQ-5D-5L demonstrates high reliability and known-group validity for measuring health-related quality of life in healthy adolescents and those with major mental disorders in Ethiopia.
Assessment of the psychometric properties and acceptability of candidate EQ-5D-5L hearing bolt-on questions in adults with cochlear implants.

This study investigates the impact of questionnaire layout (item-by-item vs. grid format) on EQ-HWB-9 measurement properties and compares two proposed EQ-HWB VAS versions in a representative Hong Kong general population sample.

This study evaluates the measurement properties of EQ-5D-5L with a breathing bolt-on in older adults with influenza-like illness and examines age-related differences in instrument performance across age subgroups.
